papers.title: AB027. Paraneoplastic diseases in patients with thymic epithelial tumours: findings from the nation-wide Danish thymic epithelial tumor database.
papers.abstract: Patients with thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are predisposed to autoimmune dis-eases, immunodeficiencies, and extrathymic malignancies. Still, the timing of these conditions relative to TET diagnosis and their prognostic significance remain poorly characterized. This nationwide study included all Danish patients diagnosed with TETs from 2015 to 2020. Data on demographics, tumor subtype, autoimmune diseases, immunodeficiencies, malig-nancies, follow-up, and survival were collected from electronic medical records. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize patient characteristics and disease chronology, while Kaplan-Meier analyses and log-rank tests were applied to assess associating with survival. Among 282 patients with a median age of 66 years, thymoma accounted for 85% of cases, thymic carcinoma for 14%, and thymic neuroendocrine tumors for 1.4%. Prior to TET diagnosis, 105 (37.2%) patients had a previous cancer diagnosis and 88 (31.2%) had autoim-mune disease. Over a median follow-up of 65 months, 33 (11.7%) patients developed new auto-immune diseases, and 41 (14.5%) patients developed new extrathymic cancers. The pattern of malignancies differed over time, with skin and colorectal cancers predominating before TET diagnosis, while lymphoma and prostate cancer were most frequent afterward. Myasthenia gravis was the leading autoimmune disease both before and after TET diagnosis, while Good's syndrome occurred only after diagnosis in six patients. Pre-existing autoimmune disease and pre-existing extrathymic cancer were not significantly associated with overall survival. A substantial burden of autoimmune and malignant disease was observed among patients with TETs, predominated by myasthenia gravis. Pre-existing paraneoplastic diseases were not associated with survival. A trend was observed in the incidence of certain disorders suggesting a shift in the pattern of developed paraneoplastic diseases after TET diagnosis.

papers.title: Typical Carcinoid Tumor of the Lung: A Case Report Demonstrating Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Database Analysis.
papers.abstract: Typical lung carcinoid tumors are classified as well-differentiated, low-grade (G1) neuroendocrine neoplasms. This case study details the clinical course, diagnostic complexity, and definitive management of a 41-year-old African American male diagnosed with a histologically confirmed typical carcinoid (G1) that manifested a highly aggressive anatomical phenotype. Key features included bulky multi-station ipsilateral mediastinal lymph node metastasis (N2 disease), prevalent lymphovascular invasion, and direct phrenic nerve involvement. Following definitive surgical resection (left upper lobe segmentectomy), the disease was pathologically staged as pT2a N2 M0 (Stage IIIA).

papers.title: Association of fatty acid binding protein 4 with altered immune composition and ferroptosis related signatures in metastatic medullary thyroid cancer.
papers.abstract: Medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) has a relatively poor prognosis mainly attributed to its early metastasis. This study aimed to investigate the expression pattern of fatty acid binding protein 4 (FABP4) and its relationship to the immune and metabolic landscape in metastatic MTC. Tissues for single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis were obtained from Jurong Hospital, to reveal the immune landscape of metastatic MTC. Gene expression profiles from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were analyzed through weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), differential expression gene (DEG) analysis and functional enrichment. Tissues for immunohistochemistry (IHC) were from The First Affiliated Hospital with Nanjing Medical University. scRNA-seq showed that the lymph node cellular composition diverged from that of primary tissues, with an increased proportions of B cells versus T/natural killer cells. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed substantial enrichment pathways including fatty acid metabolism. After discriminating tumor cells by inferCNV and CopyKAT, FABP4 was more enriched in metastatic than in primary tumor cells, which was in line with IHC staining. Also, the module incorporating the six key genes including FABP4, which were found to be upregulated in metastatic MTC by DEGs with WGCNA. Functional enrichment displayed that the differential genes were associated with ferroptosis and fatty acid metabolism. The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) data presented the correlation between FABP4 and glutathione peroxidase 4. Elevated FABP4 expression is associated with metastatic MTC, concurrent with altered immune cell composition and enrichment of ferroptosis related pathways. These findings identified FABP4 as a potential biomarker of metastasis, which is useful for the completement of theoretical basis and the guidance of personalized therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: A retrospective analysis of TACE-based multimodal liver-directed therapy for unresectable gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine carcinoma with liver metastases.
papers.abstract: Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is widely used for liver metastases from well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors, which are typically hypervascular. In contrast, gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine carcinoma liver metastases (GEP-NECLM) may be less hypervascular, raising uncertainty regarding the role of embolization-based therapy in this population. Nevertheless, TACE has also demonstrated antitumor activity in relatively hypovascular liver metastases, such as colorectal liver metastases. In clinical practice, TACE may also be combined with hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC) as part of a multimodal liver-directed strategy. We therefore hypothesized that TACE-based multimodal liver-directed therapy could provide intrahepatic antitumor activity in patients with unresectable GEP-NECLM and aimed to evaluate its efficacy, safety, and prognostic factors. Patients with unresectable GEP-NECLM who underwent TACE-based multimodal liver-directed therapy between February 2012 and June 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Pathological diagnoses were reassessed according to the 2019 World Health Organization classification. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS), defined as the time from the first TACE session to death from any cause. Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), defined as the time from the first TACE session to progressive disease in any organ or all-cause mortality; hepatic progression-free survival (hPFS), defined as the time from the first TACE session to intrahepatic disease progression or all-cause mortality; objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), and safety. A total of 34 patients were included; 24 (70.6%) received TACE in combination with HAIC, and 29 (85.3%) had received at least one line of prior systemic therapy. The ORR and DCR were 41.2% and 76.5%, respectively. After a median follow-up of 45.1 months, the median PFS was 4.4 months, the median hPFS was 5.5 months and the median OS was 10.8 months. Colorectal primary site was independently associated with shorter PFS, with a hazard ratio (HR) of 3.189 (P=0.01). Ki-67 proliferation index (Ki-67) ≥55% (HR =6.172; P=0.006) was independently associated with worse OS. A total of 34 patients underwent 60 interventional treatment sessions. The treatment showed an acceptable safety profile, with no 30-day mortality or hepatic decompensation. Post-embolization syndrome was the most common treatment-emergent adverse event, occurring in 32 of 60 sessions (53.3%). All adverse events were manageable with symptomatic treatment. TACE-based multimodal liver-directed therapy was associated with measurable intrahepatic antitumor activity and an acceptable safety profile in patients with unresectable GEP-NECLM. Colorectal primary site was independently associated with shorter PFS, whereas a Ki-67 ≥55% was independently associated with worse OS. These findings require further validation in larger prospective studies.

papers.title: Diagnostic approaches for neuroendocrine tumors of unknown primary: the role of surgical exploration and advances in molecular profiling.
The elusive culprit: a renal neuroendocrine tumor unmasked by ectopic Cushing syndrome.
papers.abstract: The case provides insight into the diagnostics and management of ectopic Cushing syndrome caused by the ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) secretion by a primary renal neuroendocrine tumor (RenNET), an exceptionally rare cause of endogenous hypercortisolism.

papers.title: From risk factors to individualized prediction: development and internal validation of a machine learning model for early identification of postoperative pneumonia after lung cancer surgery.
papers.abstract: Postoperative pneumonia (POP) remains one of the most common infectious complications following lung cancer surgery and is associated with substantial morbidity. Although several risk factors for POP have been identified, clinically applicable approaches for early individualized risk stratification remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate machine learning models for early prediction of POP using routinely available perioperative variables. In this prospective single-center cohort study, 258 consecutive patients undergoing pulmonary resection for non-small cell lung cancer or pulmonary carcinoid tumors were screened, of whom 200 were included in the final study cohort. POP was defined by newly developed postoperative radiographic abnormalities accompanied by clinical signs of infection requiring antibiotic therapy. Machine learning models, including logistic regression (LR), Naïve Bayes (NB), random forest (RF), and XGBoost (XGB), were developed to predict POP using demographic, clinical, laboratory, surgical, and postoperative day 1 radiographic variables. Model performance was assessed using nested leave-one-out cross-validation and quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). A nomogram was constructed from the best-performing model to facilitate individualized risk estimation. Different decision thresholds were explored to evaluate clinically relevant trade-offs between sensitivity and specificity. POP occurred in 47 of 200 patients (23.5%), while no POP-related mortality was observed. LR demonstrated the best predictive performance (AUROC 0.701±0.070), followed by NB (0.698±0.103), RF (0.656±0.217), and XGB (0.589±0.179). The most influential predictors included advanced age, perioperative changes in C-reactive protein concentration (ΔCRP), elevated preoperative CRP levels, prolonged operative duration, and abnormal postoperative day 1 chest radiographic findings. At a decision threshold of 25%, the model correctly identified 25 of 47 POP cases (53.2%), whereas increasing the threshold to 32.5% reduced false-positive classifications from 42 to 24 at the expense of missing an additional four POP cases. Machine learning models based on routinely available perioperative variables enabled early individualized prediction of POP following lung cancer surgery. LR provided the best balance between predictive performance, stability, and interpretability, allowing the development of an interpretable nomogram for individualized risk estimation. The model may have potential to support risk-adapted postoperative surveillance and more efficient allocation of healthcare resources; however, external validation is required before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Pediatric gigantism due to ectopic growth hormone releasing hormone secretion from a metastatic bronchial neuroendocrine tumor.
papers.abstract: Pediatric gigantism due to ectopic secretion of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) is exceptionally rare. Most pediatric reports have involved pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors in the context of multiple endocrine neoplasia 1 (MEN1). We describe a female patient diagnosed at 9 years of age with a typical bronchial neuroendocrine tumor and subsequently found to have diffuse hepatic and skeletal metastases, accelerated linear growth, and acromegalic features. Evaluation demonstrated markedly elevated plasma GHRH, growth hormone, and insulin-like growth factor 1, with diffuse pituitary hyperplasia on magnetic resonance imaging and no discrete pituitary adenoma. Genetic testing for MEN1 was negative. Management required repeated surgery, first-generation somatostatin analogs, dopamine agonist therapy, pegvisomant, pasireotide, and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy with lutetium-177 DOTA-Tyr3-octreotate. Pasireotide achieved improved biochemical control, while peptide receptor radionuclide therapy contributed to long-term structural stability. After 23 years of follow-up, the patient remains clinically well with stable tumor burden and controlled somatotropic axis. This case highlights the natural history of a pediatric-onset GHRH-secreting neuroendocrine tumor and highlights the efficacy of aggressive, multidisciplinary management in achieving long-term survival.

papers.title: Prognostic prediction of pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinoma using a transformer-based artificial intelligence model: a two-center retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinomas (pNECs) are a rare and heterogeneous group of malignancies, ranging from low-grade carcinoids to high-grade small-cell lung carcinoma (SCLC) and large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC). Prognostic tools for these tumors are scarce and have rarely been validated in external cohorts. This study aimed to develop a Transformer-based prognostic prediction model for pNEC and validate it in an independent external cohort, to improve survival estimation and support individualized treatment decisions. This retrospective two-center cohort study included 823 patients with surgically resected pNEC (2001-2023). Models were developed in Center 1 (n=374; randomly split 8:2 into training and internal test sets) and externally validated in an independent Center 2 cohort (n=449). Three algorithms-logistic regression (LR), decision tree (DT), and the Transformer-based tabular foundation model TabPFN-were compared for estimating overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) at 1-, 3-, and 5-year landmarks, with evaluation by receiver operating characteristic, calibration, and decision curve analyses, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis for interpretability. TabPFN achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) in most tasks in both test sets, with task-dependent exceptions: in the internal test set, logistic regression performed best for 1-year OS (AUC 0.885), while TabPFN performed best for the remaining tasks, including 3-year OS (0.880), overall DFS (0.810), and 1-year DFS (0.892); in the external test set, TabPFN remained best for 1- and 3-year OS and for overall, 1-, and 3-year DFS (0.747-0.802), whereas logistic regression performed best for 5-year OS and DFS. External calibration was less satisfactory. Disease stage, pathological subtype, and age were the key prognostic predictors, and TabPFN was more accurate for low-grade subtypes. SHAP analysis quantified the contribution of each feature and made the model interpretable. The Transformer-based model improves survival estimation in pNEC, with task-dependent advantages over conventional methods and confirmed transportability to an independent institutional cohort. Prospective multicenter validation and calibration refinement are needed before broader clinical use.

papers.title: Central-type primitive neuroectodermal tumor of the uterus: Case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: Primitive neuroectodermal tumors (PNETs) arising in the uterus, particularly those classified as the central-type (cPNET), are exceedingly rare. To date, approximately 30 cases of uterine cPNET have been reported, and their clinicopathological features remain poorly characterized. These tumors typically present as highly aggressive small round cell neoplasms with variable neuroectodermal differentiation, often posing significant diagnostic challenges owing to their overlap with other uterine malignancies, including neuroendocrine carcinoma, endometrial stromal sarcoma, and undifferentiated carcinoma. Here, we report a rare case of uterine cPNET characterized by a diffuse small round cell morphology and prominent neuroendocrine differentiation. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated positivity for synaptophysin, INSM1, and CD56, whereas markers associated with Ewing's sarcoma (CD99, FLI1 and NKX2.2) were negative. Next-generation sequencing revealed no Ewing sarcoma breakpoint region 1 rearrangements, supporting the exclusion of peripheral PNET. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of uterine tumors with neuroectodermal differentiation and expands the current morphological and immunophenotypic spectra of this entity. Accurate recognition requires the integration of histopathology, immunoprofile, and molecular findings, with particular attention paid to the differential diagnosis of other high-grade uterine malignancies.

papers.title: Ectopic Parathyroid Adenoma Mimicking a Vagal Paraganglioma on Somatostatin Receptor PET.
Tensile stress enhances osteogenic differentiation of rat bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells in a PC12 co-culture model through soluble-factor signaling.
papers.abstract: Mechanical stimulation and neural regulation are critical for bone repair, yet how neural cells modulate mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) osteogenic differentiation under mechanical cues remains unclear. MSCs and pheochromocytoma cell 12 (PC12) cells were indirectly co-cultured in a Transwell system, with tensile stress (TS) applied exclusively to the MSCs. MSC osteogenic differentiation, Wnt/β-catenin signaling-related molecules, and neurotrophic factors were evaluated. IWR-1 was used to assess the involvement of Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Conditioned medium (CM) from TS-treated MSC/PC12 co-cultures was applied to PC12 to assess proliferation, neuronal-like differentiation, and paracrine activity. CM from these treated PC12 was then applied to MSCs to assess its effects on osteogenic differentiation. TS enhanced alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, matrix mineralization, and osteogenic marker expression in MSCs co-cultured with PC12, accompanied by increased Wnt3a and β-catenin expression; these effects were attenuated by IWR-1. TS also increased nerve growth factor (NGF) and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) expression in MSCs and their levels in co-culture CM. CM from TS-treated MSC/PC12 co-cultures stimulated PC12 proliferation, neurite outgrowth, neuronal-like differentiation, and secretion of vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) and calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP). In turn, CM collected from PC12 after exposure to TS-treated MSC/PC12 co-culture CM further enhanced MSC osteogenic differentiation. TS enhanced MSC osteogenic differentiation in the PC12 co-culture model and was accompanied by soluble-factor-associated responses between MSCs and PC12. The changes in Wnt3a and β-catenin expression, together with the inhibitory effect of IWR-1, suggest an association between Wnt/β-catenin signaling-related responses and MSC osteogenic differentiation.

papers.title: Age reshapes selection on melanoma driver mutations.
papers.abstract: Aging is a major risk factor for melanoma. However, it is unclear whether aging fuels tumor evolution by altering mutation rates, changing the microenvironmentally induced selection on drivers, or both. We analyzed 5472 melanomas, estimating how selection on individual variants changes with patient age while accounting for differing neutral mutation rates. Neutral mutation rates increased only modestly with age; ultraviolet damage remained predominant, but endogenous processes increasingly contributed to older tumors. In contrast, selection on major drivers was strongly age dependent: The advantage of BRAF V600E declined precipitously with age, whereas NRAS Q61 mutations gained advantage. TERT promoter mutations became more frequent, yet less advantageous. Aging therefore reshapes melanoma evolution primarily by altering selection, motivating age-conscious evaluation of clinical biomarkers and therapies.

papers.title: Tinostamustine-nivolumab therapy is associated with antigen-specific cellular and humoral immune responses in heavily pre-treated patients with advanced melanoma.
papers.abstract: ENIgMA is a phase IB trial (NCT03903458; SNCTP000003243) evaluating the safety and preliminary activity of the first-in-class alkylating deacetylase inhibitor tinostamustine in combination with nivolumab (3 mg/kg) in patients with predominantly immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-resistant, advanced melanoma. We conducted this longitudinal immune monitoring study in 15 of the 17 enrolled patients to characterize systemic immunologic changes associated with an immunomodulatory dose of tinostamustine. We have previously demonstrated that combination of tinostamustine with nivolumab was able to induce disease stabilization in 54% and confirmed partial responses in 23% of evaluable patients. Peripheral blood samples collected longitudinally during treatment were analysed by flow cytometry, serum antigen-specific IgG enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and intracellular cytokine staining following ex vivo peptide stimulation. Longitudinal flow cytometric analyses demonstrated dynamic changes in peripheral immune subsets, including T cells, natural killer (NK) cells and monocytes, suggesting ongoing immune engagement during tinostamustine-nivolumab therapy. In progressors, elevated baseline lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels significantly and inversely correlated with circulating T cell frequencies, indicating distinct immune profiles associated with poor clinical outcome. Antigen-specific adaptive immune responses were detectable despite extensive prior treatment and high tumour burden. CD4+ T cell responses, particularly TNFα-associated responses directed against melanoma-associated antigens, represented the dominant cellular immune activation pattern. Additionally, treatment related increases in melanoma-associated antigen-specific IgG responses were also observed in several patients. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that immunomodulatory doses of tinostamustine in combination with nivolumab are linked with preserved adaptive immune competence and detectable cellular and humoral immune activation in heavily pre-treated patients with advanced melanoma.

papers.title: Clinical Characteristics of Mediastinal Paragangliomas: A retrospective study.
papers.abstract: Studies focusing on mediastinal paragangliomas are limited. In this study, we describe the clinical, pathological, and genetic characteristics of mediastinal paragangliomas. Clinical data from all patients with extrapericardial mediastinal paragangliomas at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Germline variants were assessed using next-generation sequencing and Sanger sequencing of blood samples. Patients were grouped according to genetic variants and tumor location, and clinical characteristics were compared. 22 patients (male:female ratio, 8:14) were included in the study, with a mean age of 41.4 years. Hypertension was present in 16 patients (72.7%), and 13 (59.1%) exhibited typical catecholamine-related symptoms. Tumors were located in the anterior, middle, and posterior mediastinum in 1 (4.5%), 4 (18.2%), and 17 (77.3%) cases, with an average size of 5.3±1.7 cm. Multiple tumors were identified in 6 patients. Catecholamine-producing tumors were observed in 17/21 (81.0%) patients. Surgical resection was performed in 20 (90.9%) patients. No postoperative local recurrences were observed. Metastasis occurred in 2/18 (11.1%) cases. Eleven patients underwent genetic testing; six harbored SDHx mutations. Compared with anterior and middle mediastinal tumors, posterior mediastinal tumors were associated with higher rates of typical symptoms (12/17 vs. 1/5, p = 0.043) and catecholamine-producing function (17/17 vs. 0/4, p < 0.001), as well as higher levels of 24-hour urinary norepinephrine (5.10 × ULN vs. 0.56 × ULN, p = 0.037). Mediastinal paragangliomas are rare and are frequently associated with SDHx variants. Posterior mediastinal tumors are predominantly functional and noradrenergic; recognizing these features may facilitate diagnosis.

papers.title: Revisiting the Role of Chemotherapy in Advanced Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
papers.abstract: Chemotherapy has been always considered scarcely or completely ineffective in the treatment of metastatic and progressive MTC. We report the case of a 45-year-old man who underwent total thyroidectomy and lymphadenectomy in May 2023 for bilateral MTC with extrathyroidal extension and 2/23 metastatic lymph nodes. Germline and somatic RET genetic analysis were negative. From July 2023 to February 2024 tumour markers progressively increased and a 18F-DOPA PET/CT revealed metastases in the cervical region and mediastinal inlet. Therefore, cabozantinib was started, obtaining a partial response, but after 1 year of treatment disease progression at the cervicomediastinal level was documented, despite dosage increase. Thus, an off-label treatment with lenvatinib was started, achieving a transient stabilization. In October 2025, a further disease progression was diagnosed. The patient started off-label chemotherapy consisting of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) 400 mg/m2 intravenous (IV) bolus, followed by 5-FU 2400 mg/m2 as a 48-hour infusion, combined with dacarbazine 800 mg/m2 IV in 30 minutes, every 14 days for the first month and then every 21 days for the following months. Chemotherapy was very well tolerated. At the last visit, after 17 cycles, tumour markers returned to the normal range (CA 19-9 22.9 kU/L, CEA 2.5 μg/L) and PET/CT scanning showed a complete response. In conclusion, this case shows that, although treatment with multikinase inhibitors is actually the first choice for advanced RET-wild-type MTC, conventional chemotherapy can be effective at least in some patients and should always be considered, especially in case of failure of other approaches.

papers.title: Dihydrotanshinone I in Paired Vemurafenib-Sensitive and Resistant A375 Melanoma Cells.
papers.abstract: Acquired resistance limits the response to vemurafenib in melanoma. This study investigated dihydrotanshinone I (DHT) in parental A375 cells and a vemurafenib-resistant derivative (A375R). An exploratory computational workflow combined target prediction, survival associations, tumor-versus-normal expression comparisons, dependency screening, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) Cox regression, and random survival forests. Heat shock protein 90 alpha family class A member 1 (HSP90AA1) and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) were prioritized for cellular testing. Cellular thermal shift assays showed DHT-associated thermal stabilization, and combined small interfering RNA depletion produced greater phenotypic effects than single-target depletion. Eight drug combinations yielded Chou-Talalay combination indices of 0.520-0.940 in A375R cells. Transcriptional changes and lipid-peroxidation readouts were consistent with altered resistance-associated and oxidative-stress programs. Together, these findings support further investigation of HSP90AA1 and STAT3 in the response of resistant melanoma cells to DHT.

papers.title: α-Mangostin-Loaded Gold Nanorod-Integrated MOF Nanoplatform for Photoacoustic Imaging-Guided Photothermal Therapy of Melanoma Involving Pyroptosis-Related Signaling.
papers.abstract: Melanoma remains a highly aggressive malignancy with limited therapeutic options, largely due to poor tumor selectivity and acquired resistance to conventional treatments in advanced disease. This study aimed to develop a gold nanorod (AuNR)-integrated metal-organic framework (MOF) theranostic nanoplatform for photoacoustic imaging-guided photothermal therapy of melanoma and to investigate its association with pyroptosis-related signaling. The α-MG/AuNR@ZIF-8/FA-PEG nanoplatform was rationally engineered to co-deliver α-mangostin (α-MG) and AuNRs within a pH-responsive ZIF-8 matrix, with folate-PEG surface modification to enhance cellular uptake. Physicochemical properties were characterized by TEM, DLS, and FTIR. Drug release profiles, photothermal conversion efficiency, hemocompatibility, and short-term in vivo tolerability were systematically evaluated. In vitro cytotoxicity and cellular uptake were assessed in A375 melanoma cells, and in vivo antitumor efficacy was validated in tumor-bearing mice. The pyroptosis-related signaling pathway was investigated by Western blotting. The nanoplatform exhibited favorable colloidal stability, pH-responsive controlled drug release, and excellent photothermal performance, with a hydrodynamic diameter of approximately 212.1 nm, a zeta potential of approximately -22 mV, an α-MG loading capacity of 21.89 ± 0.02%, and a peak temperature of approximately 56.5 °C under 808 nm laser irradiation (1.0 W/cm2). FA-PEG modification was associated with enhanced cellular uptake, while time-dependent tumor accumulation of the nanoplatform was observed in vivo. The combined treatment produced greater antitumor effects than the tested comparator groups, with an approximately 70% tumor growth inhibition rate. Mechanistically, treatment was associated with increased oxidative stress, activation of the canonical NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD pyroptosis-related pathway, and enhanced cell death. AuNR-mediated photothermal heating further strengthened these responses, suggesting that the improved antitumor efficacy may involve the combined effects of α-MG-induced oxidative stress, photothermal injury, and activation of pyroptosis-related signaling. This multifunctional nanoplatform integrates α-MG delivery, real-time photoacoustic imaging, and controlled photothermal activation, and its antitumor effects were associated with activation of pyroptosis-related signaling. These findings support further investigation of this platform for image-guided melanoma therapy.

papers.title: Beyond Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: A Narrative Review of the Radiological and Endoscopic Features of Solid Pancreatic Neoplasms.
papers.abstract: Solid pancreatic neoplasms comprise a heterogeneous group of tumors with distinct histopathological characteristics, biological behaviors, and therapeutic implications. Although pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is the predominant malignancy, non-ductal neoplasms, including pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma (PACC), pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PanNETs), solid pseudopapillary neoplasms (SPNs), and pancreatoblastoma, represent important diagnostic alternatives. This narrative review aims to summarize and compare the radiological and endoscopic features of solid pancreatic neoplasms, emphasizing their differential diagnosis and the contribution of endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided tissue acquisition to diagnostic characterization. A narrative review of the literature was conducted, focusing on studies addressing CT, MRI, conventional and contrast-enhanced EUS, elastography, and EUS-guided tissue acquisition in the characterization and differential diagnosis of solid pancreatic tumors. PDAC typically demonstrates infiltrative growth and reduced enhancement, whereas non-ductal neoplasms may exhibit well-defined margins and variable vascular patterns. PACC may present as a well-circumscribed mass with heterogeneous enhancement and areas of cystic degeneration, while PanNETs frequently demonstrate hypervascularity, and SPNs often exhibit mixed solid and cystic components. However, substantial imaging overlap limits reliable histological differentiation. Beyond the morphological and vascular characterization provided by EUS, EUS-guided fine-needle biopsy (EUS-FNB), combined with histological and immunohistochemical analysis, plays a crucial role in establishing a definitive diagnosis, particularly for uncommon neoplasms. Emerging technologies, including radiomics and artificial intelligence (AI), offer promising opportunities for improving diagnostic characterization. Accurate differentiation of solid pancreatic neoplasms requires an integrated approach combining cross-sectional imaging, EUS, and histopathological assessment. Recognizing characteristic imaging patterns and understanding their limitations may improve diagnostic accuracy and guide appropriate tissue acquisition and therapeutic decision-making.

papers.title: Pheochromocytoma masquerading as fulminant myocarditis with marked interleukin-6 elevation: a case report.
papers.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a rare cause of cardiogenic shock with diverse cardiovascular manifestations. Although catecholamine-induced cardiomyopathy is well recognized, presentations closely resembling fulminant myocarditis are uncommon and diagnostically challenging. The role of cytokine-mediated inflammatory activation in such presentations is not well defined. A previously healthy woman in her 30s presented with fever, ventricular arrhythmias, and severe left ventricular dysfunction, rapidly progressing to cardiogenic shock requiring venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and Impella support. Fulminant myocarditis was initially suspected based on clinical, electrocardiographic, and biomarker findings, and immunomodulatory therapy was initiated. Although transient improvement was observed, endomyocardial biopsy showed minimal inflammatory infiltration. Subsequent computed tomography revealed a left adrenal mass, and biochemical testing confirmed markedly elevated catecholamines. Notably, interleukin-6 (IL-6) was also markedly elevated relative to C-reactive protein. Despite initiation of α-blockade, the patient developed recurrent haemodynamic collapse, necessitating emergency adrenalectomy. Pathological examination confirmed a necrotic pheochromocytoma, but the patient died of refractory multiorgan failure. This case illustrates how pheochromocytoma can closely mimic fulminant myocarditis, with a risk of diagnostic anchoring. The coexistence of marked IL-6 elevation and catecholamine excess raises the possibility of concomitant inflammatory activation, although a causal role of IL-6 cannot be established. Recognition of this pattern is important to prompt reconsideration of endocrine aetiologies in myocarditis-like cardiogenic shock.

papers.title: Solitary Neurofibroma in the Submental Region of a 15-Year-Old Adolescent: A Case Report and Review of Literature.
papers.abstract: Neurofibroma is a benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor composed of Schwann cells and fibroblasts. It may occur sporadically or as part of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1). Solitary neurofibroma arising in the submental region of an adolescent is extremely rare. We report a case of a solitary submental neurofibroma in a 15-year-old male and highlight its diagnostic and management implications. A 15-year-old adolescent boy presented with a chronic, painless right submental swelling that had been present for one year and had enlarged over the preceding three months. Clinical examination revealed a rubbery, nontender, approximately 3×3×4 cm mass without skin changes or systemic symptoms. There was no personal or family history suggestive of NF1, neural tumors, or pheochromocytoma. Ultrasound and CT imaging showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass consistent with a benign neurogenic tumor. The mass was completely excised via a submental incision. Histopathological examination confirmed a solitary neurofibroma with Schwann cell and fibroblast proliferation within a collagen matrix, Antoni A and B patterns, and positive S-100 immunostaining, with no evidence of malignancy. The postoperative course was uneventful, and tongue and floor-of-mouth function were preserved. Solitary submental neurofibroma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of submental masses in adolescents, even in the absence of NF1 features. Complete surgical excision is the treatment of choice and allows definitive histopathological diagnosis. A thorough evaluation for NF1 is recommended to guide long-term management and follow-up.

papers.title: Primary-site variation in recorded metastatic patterns and survival associations in extrapulmonary poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Extrapulmonary poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma (EP-PD-NEC) is aggressive and heterogeneous. Our primary objective was to assess primary-site differences in bone, brain, liver, and lung metastases recorded at diagnosis. Secondary analyses examined prognostic effect modification and the incremental predictive information in these variables. We analyzed Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results data from 2010-2023. Strict EP-PD-NEC was defined by ICD-O-3 codes 8013 and 8041-8045. Bone, brain, liver, and lung metastases recorded at diagnosis were evaluated using modified Poisson regression with individual-level heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors. Overall survival (OS) was analyzed with multivariable Cox models containing primary-site-by-organ interactions. Associations identified in 2010-2017 were reassessed in 2018-2022. Four prespecified ridge-penalized Cox models were developed and temporally evaluated in distant-stage cases with complete four-organ status. Primary prevalence analyses included patients with known status for the organ analyzed; sensitivity analyses recoded unknown status as negative or used multiple imputation. Among 6,044 eligible patients, 5,820 (96.3%) had complete four-organ information and 2,356 had at least one recorded organ involved. Recorded metastatic prevalence differed across six primary-site groups for every organ (all false-discovery-rate-adjusted P<0.001). Versus genitourinary primaries, pancreatic primaries had higher adjusted prevalence of liver (prevalence ratio [PR] 3.80, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.39-4.25) and brain metastases (PR 2.86, 95% CI 1.75-4.66). An increasing recorded four-organ count was associated with shorter OS. The global primary-site-by-organ interaction was significant (likelihood-ratio χ²=43.49, 20 df, P = 0.00176), but the full interaction matrix added negligible temporal predictive value (ΔC-index=0.00169). In 1,374 later-period patients, the spectrum model had a C-index of 0.607 (95% CI 0.588-0.624), a 12-month area under the curve of 0.672 (95% CI 0.639-0.706), and a Brier score of 0.196 (95% CI 0.185-0.207). Compared with the four-organ-count model, paired bootstrap differences were 0.0085 (95% CI 0.0035-0.0139) for the C-index, 0.0119 (95% CI 0.0033-0.0231) for 12-month AUC, and -0.0020 (95% CI -0.0038 to -0.0004) for the Brier score. Missing-status analyses produced similar prevalence estimates. Recorded metastatic patterns differed by primary site in EP-PD-NEC. Organ identity added little predictive information beyond the recorded four-organ count, and site-by-organ interactions yielded negligible improvement. Overall discrimination remained modest.

papers.title: Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Thyroid Cancer: Review of Preclinical and Human Data.
papers.abstract: Preclinical rodent studies showing a dose-dependent increase in thyroid C-cell hyperplasia and neoplasia with Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists (GLP-1RAs), led the United States Federal Drug Administration to require a boxed warning contraindicating GLP-1RAs for patients with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or in patients with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome. However, neither primate oncogenicity studies nor patient clinical trials showed C-cell stimulation, calling into question the relevance of rodent models to humans. Indeed, rodents have a high rate of spontaneous thyroid C-cell tumors, a higher number of thyroid C-cells and GLP-1 receptors and use a different pathway from humans in MTC oncogenesis. Although, the majority of meta-analyses of randomized clinical trials and cohort studies using administrative, electronic medical record and/or registry databases report no clear association between GLP-1RA use and thyroid cancer development, pharmacovigilance database studies do demonstrate a positive relationship; however, this association can only be inferred as a possible signal rather than causation and is likely due to notoriety or reporting bias. Additionally, analysis of the overall trends of thyroid cancer incidence in the U.S. since the release of GLP-1RAs for patient use in 2005 show an early increase, probably due to overdiagnosis of papillary carcinoma (PTC); however, the relative proportion of MTC has actually decreased. Because the preponderance of data does not support a causative relationship between GLP-1RA use and MTC (or PTC), we conclude that the need for the boxed warning about the risk of C-cell neoplasia is no longer necessary.

papers.title: The efficacy and safety of endoscopic resection for multiple rectal neuroendocrine tumors: a retrospective cohort study from a tertiary center.
papers.abstract: Multiple rectal neuroendocrine tumors (MR-NETs) are rare. There is no consensus on their characteristics and treatment. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of endoscopic resection (ER) for MR-NETs. We performed a retrospective review of 24 patients with 57 rectal NETs who underwent ER at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University. Baseline information, procedure-related characteristics and postoperative outcomes were analyzed. The mean maximal diameter was 8.2 ± 4.5 mm, with 43 lesions < 10 mm and 14 lesions ≥ 10 mm. Seventeen patients had 2 lesions, 6 patients had 3 lesions and 1 patient had 5 lesions. There were 53 lesions treated by endoscopic submucosal dissection, 2 lesions treated by endoscopic mucosal resection, and 2 lesions treated by endoscopic submucosal excavation. The en bloc resection rate and technical success rate were both 100%. There were no delayed bleeding or perforation. All patients were eventually discharged safely, with a mean post-procedure hospital stay of 1.81 ± 0.48 days. Tumor grade was G1 in 54 (94.7%) lesions and G2 in 3 lesions (5.3%). Positive margins were found in 10 lesions, including 2 lesions (3.5%) with lateral margin involvement, and 8 cases (14.0%) with basal margin involvement. Mean follow-up was 34.96 ± 23.20 months, with only 3 local recurrences which were successfully managed by salvage ER. There were no recurrences in the 10 lesions with positive margins. ER is a safe and effective technique for small MR-NETs. Positive resection margins do not appear to adversely affect the prognosis of small MR-NETs. Salvage ER may be a viable option in recurrent cases.

papers.title: Chemodectoma Arising From the Abdominal Aorta in a 9-Year-Old Female Dog: Clinical, Histopathological and Immunohistochemstric Study.
papers.abstract: Chemodectomas are uncommon, typically benign neoplasms derived from paraganglionic chemoreceptor tissues, most frequently arising in the heart base or carotid bodies of brachycephalic dogs. This report documents a detailed pathological description of a chemodectoma originating from the abdominal aorta in a non-human species, representing, to our knowledge, the first case specifically characterized by its origin at the aortic trifurcation, thereby expanding the recognized anatomical spectrum of this tumour entity. A 9-year-old spayed female terrier was presented with persistent panting, recent-onset obesity following previous cachexia, and a complex clinical history including polyuria/polydipsia and pyoderma. Haematological and biochemical analyses revealed a regenerative anaemia, leucocytosis, and biochemical indicators suggestive of cholestasis and potential endocrinopathy. Advanced imaging identified a solitary, well-demarcated, highly vascular abdominal mass closely associated with the aortic trifurcation. Given the tumour's inaccessibility and pronounced vascularity, cytological confirmation via fine needle aspiration was precluded due to haemorrhagic risk, necessitating exploratory laparotomy. Intraoperatively, the mass was unresectable because of its anatomical relationships and the prohibitive risk of catastrophic haemorrhage. Humane euthanasia was subsequently elected. Histopathological evaluation demonstrated a lobulated neoplasm composed of pleomorphic neuroendocrine cells, with low mitotic activity and an absence of necrosis or haemorrhage. Immunohistochemistry confirmed strong, diffuse synaptophysin reactivity and focal neuron-specific enolase positivity, while chromogranin A and S100 protein were negative, underscoring immunophenotypic variability. This case illustrates the diagnostic complexity and therapeutic limitations posed by extra-cardiac chemodectomas in veterinary species, especially when located in unconventional anatomical sites. Limitations included the unavailability of computed tomography and lack of postoperative follow-up. This report expands the recognized clinico-pathological spectrum of chemodectomas and highlights the necessity for multidisciplinary diagnostic strategies and further research aimed at defining optimal management protocols for such rare and challenging presentations.

papers.title: Geographic Disparities in Transsphenoidal Pituitary Surgery in the State of São Paulo, Brazil: An Analysis of the Public Healthcare System.
papers.abstract: To analyze the surgical volume, geographic distribution, healthcare indicators, and costs of transsphenoidal surgeries performed within the public healthcare system in the state of São Paulo over a 15-year period. A retrospective study based on publicly available secondary data obtained from the São Paulo State Health Department TabNet database. Hospitalizations related to transsphenoidal hypophysectomy performed between 2010 and 2024 were included. Surgical volume, regional distribution, length of hospital stay, intensive care unit stay (ICU), mortality, and costs were evaluated. A total of 4,086 surgeries were performed, with an annual mean of 272 ± 53 procedures, predominantly concentrated in Region 1 (68%). The mean hospital length of stay was 9.4 ± 0.9 days, showing a decreasing trend over time in some regions, whereas the mean ICU stay was 2.1 ± 0.3 days, with an increasing trend statewide. Significant regional differences were observed regarding hospital length of stay, ICU stay, and costs (p < 0.001). The mean cost per hospitalization was US$ 852 ± 93, with an upward trend throughout the study period. Overall mortality was 1.1%, remaining low and stable over time. Considerable heterogeneity was observed among high-volume centers, with differences in healthcare and financial indicators. Transsphenoidal surgeries in the state of São Paulo are concentrated in higher-volume regions and centers, with substantial heterogeneity in healthcare and financial indicators. Nevertheless, mortality remains low, reinforcing the safety of this procedure within the public healthcare system.

papers.title: [Atypical Pulmonary Carcinoid with Multiple Distant Metastases Treated with Primary Tumor Resection].
papers.abstract: A 73-year-old man presented with cough and was found to have a tumor in the right lower lobe associated with obstructive pneumonia. Chest computed tomography (CT) and fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography revealed multiple distant metastases involving the liver, lymph nodes, and bone. Bronchoscopic biopsy suggested typical pulmonary carcinoid. Although curative resection was not feasible, primary tumor resection was performed to achieve local control and prevent recurrent obstructive pneumonia. Histopathological examination demonstrated atypical pulmonary carcinoid. The patient subsequently received carboplatin plus etoposide, followed by everolimus and a somatostatin analogue after disease progression. Local control was achieved, and the patient's general condition has been maintained despite slow progression of liver metastases. This case suggests that primary tumor resection may be a useful treatment option in selected patients with metastatic atypical pulmonary carcinoid.

papers.title: Merkel cell carcinoma: A case not to miss.
Clinicopathologic characteristics and survival outcomes of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms in Peru: A 15-year retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Incidence of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (GEP-NENs) has increased globally; however, data from Latin America remain scarce. This study aimed to describe the sociodemographic and clinicopathologic characteristics, treatment modalities, survival outcomes, and prognostic factors of GEP-NENs in a 15-year single-center cohort at a national referral cancer center in Lima, Peru. We conducted a retrospective, hospital-based cohort study. Patients diagnosed with GEP-NENs at the Instituto Nacional de Enfermedades Neoplásicas (INEN) were included from 2009 to 2024, and tumors were classified according to the 2019 WHO Classification of GEP-NENs. Overall survival (OS) was estimated using Kaplan-Meier curves and compared using the log-rank test. Prognostic factors were identified through Cox proportional hazards models. Three hundred sixty-eight patients were included. The median age at diagnosis was 57 years, with a female predominance (56.2%). Most patients presented with an ECOG performance status of 0-1 (96.5%), and among patients with available disease-extent information, 64.7% had non-metastatic disease. The majority of tumors were well-differentiated (neuroendocrine tumors [NETs]) (84.2%), while 15.8% were poorly differentiated (neuroendocrine carcinomas [NECs]). The most common primary tumor sites included the rectum (39.1%), stomach (19.8%), and pancreas (18.8%). With a median follow-up of 61.9 months, the 5-year OS rate was 52%. NETs exhibited longer OS than NECs, with 5-year OS rates of 65% and 8%, respectively (log-rank p < 0.001). In the multivariable analysis, metastatic disease (aHR = 2.61, 95% CI: 1.63-4.20; p < 0.001) and poorly differentiated histology (aHR: 4.36, 95% CI: 2.59-7.31; p < 0.001) were independently associated with worse overall survival, whereas surgery (aHR: 0.25, 95% CI: 0.15-0.41; p < 0.001) and systemic treatment (aHR: 0.53, 95% CI: 0.31-0.92; p = 0.024) were associated with improved overall survival. Our findings demonstrate that GEP-NENs represent a highly heterogeneous group of neoplasms with substantial variability in clinicopathological characteristics and survival outcomes. Most patients in our cohort had well-differentiated NETs and favorable long-term survival. These findings support the need for comprehensive national registries and multicenter collaborative studies to validate our results and better characterize GEP-NENs in underrepresented Latin American populations.

papers.title: [Meat Inspection - What's Your Diagnosis?].
papers.abstract: During a meat inspection of a 12-year-old female cow, cordlike and multinodular masses were detected in the right atrium and the right ventricle. The cut surfaces of the nodules were gelatinous and yellowish. Histologically, monomorphic, spindle-shaped cells were observed, arranged in compact bundles and palisades. Immunohistochemical testing showed variable positivity for S100, vimentin, and glial fibrillary acidic protein GFAP. The findings are consistent with a peripheral nerve sheath tumor (schwannoma) of the heart. The affected organ was deemed unfit for human consumption, while the remainder of the carcass was classified as fit for human consumption.

papers.title: Interpatient and intrapatient variability in organ absorbed doses during [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy for neuroendocrine tumors.
papers.abstract: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) with lutetium-177 labeled somatostatin analogues is an established treatment for patients with advanced neuroendocrine tumors (NETs). There is growing evidence of a dose-response relationship. Considering critical organ exposure, most patients are treated with fixed administered activities. Interpatient variability in absorbed dose per administered activity is observed, highlighting the need for treatment personalization. The objective was to evaluate interpatient variability in absorbed doses to critical organs during [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy and intrapatient intercycle variability in absorbed doses to different organs across successive treatment cycles. A dosimetric analysis was performed in ten patients with metastatic NETs undergoing PRRT with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTATATE. Each patient received four treatment cycles at approximately 8-week intervals. Quantitative single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT) imaging was acquired at 6, 24, 96 and 192 hours post-injection using a Siemens Symbia Intevo Bold system. Image reconstruction and dosimetric analysis were performed using Hermia and OLINDA/EXM 2.2. Organs were segmented on CT images and propagated to subsequent time points. Absorbed doses (Gy/GBq) were calculated for the kidneys, liver, spleen, and whole body. The sum of cycle-specific D/A₀ values after four treatment cycles ranged from 1.13 to 4.21 Gy/GBq for kidneys, 0.32 to 3.97 Gy/GBq for liver, 1.49 to 3.14 Gy/GBq for spleen and 0.07 to 0.22 Gy/GBq for total body. The greatest interpatient variability was observed in the liver. Intrapatient variability (CV) was highest for the liver (13.4 ± 6.5%), followed by the spleen (9.2 ± 3.6%) and kidneys (9.1 ± 4.4%), while whole-body variability remained minimal across treatment cycles. Significant inter- and intrapatient variability in organ absorbed doses, particularly in the liver, supports the need for personalized dosimetry in [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-PRRT. These findings highlight the limitations of fixed-activity protocols and warrant further investigation of dose-toxicity relationships.

papers.title: Hepatic Epithelioid Angiosarcoma with Abberrant Synaptophysin and CDX2 Expression Mimicking Neuroendocrine/Metastatic Carcinoma: A Fatal Case Report.
papers.abstract: We report a fatal case of presumed primary hepatic epithelioid angiosarcoma (PHEA) in an 82-year-old woman with back pain, abdominal distension, and hyponatremia. Imaging showed ascites and hypodense hepatic lesions. Ascitic cytology was negative. Liver biopsy showed malignant cells with positive erythroblast transformation-specific regulated gene 1 (ERG) and cluster of differentiation 31 (CD31) on immunohistochemistry. Patchy synaptophysin and caudal-type homeobox 2 positivity initially suggested a neuroendocrine tumor but proved aberrant; negative chromogranin with ERG/CD31 positivity supported PHEA. She was transitioned to hospice care due to rapid clinical decline. This case highlights the atypical presentation, diagnostic pitfalls, and aggressive clinical course of PHEA.

papers.title: FAP-targeted [68Ga]BED003-PET compared with [18F]DOPA-PET in patients with recurrent medullary thyroid carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Molecular imaging of recurrent or advanced medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) remains clinically challenging. [18F]DOPA-PET is an established reference standard, but its sensitivity is limited and dependent on tumour burden and biomarker levels. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeted PET has emerged as a promising imaging approach across several malignancies. This study aimed to compare the detection rate and quantitative imaging characteristics of [68Ga]BED003-PET, recently known as [68Ga]OncoFAP-DOTAGA, with [18F]DOPA-PET in patients with recurrent or advanced MTC. Eight patients with histologically proven MTC and suspected recurrence or progression based on elevated calcitonin levels underwent both [18F]DOPA-PET and an additional [68Ga]BED003-PET. All patients presented with inconclusive findings in [18F]DOPA-PET. Comparative analyses were performed on a patient- and lesion-based level. Quantitative parameters included maximum and mean standardized uptake values (SUVmax/SUVmean), metabolic tumour volume (MTV), and maximum tumour-to-background ratios (TBRmax). Potential theranostic suitability was explored based on lesional FAP uptake. The median interval between PET acquisitions was 33 days (range, 7-56 days). In total, 35 tracer-avid lesions were detected. [68Ga]BED003-PET detected significantly more lesions than [18F]DOPA-PET (34/35 [97%] vs. 16/35 [46%], P < 0.001). 15 lesions (43%) were positive on both modalities, 19 (54%) were only [68Ga]BED003-positive, and 1 (2.9%) was only [18F]DOPA-positive. Quantitative analysis demonstrated significantly higher uptake and contrast for [68Ga]BED003, including higher blood-pool TBRmax than [18F]DOPA (6.02 vs. 2.23, Bonferroni adjusted P < 0.001). In this small MTC cohort, [68Ga]BED003-PET demonstrated higher lesion detection and TBRs in patients with inconsistent findings in [18F]DOPA-PET. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted.

papers.title: Second-generation ICG fusion fluorescence endoscopy in pituitary neuroendocrine tumor surgery.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the clinical feasibility of integrating second-generation real-time indocyanine green (ICG) fusion fluorescence endoscopy into routine transsphenoidal surgical workflow for pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs). Our focus was on describing the qualitative fluorescence patterns of PitNETs observed within the procedure-embedded 15-18 min delay window following administration of ICG, and evaluating the reproducibility of image interpretation. This retrospective single-center descriptive feasibility study included 26 patients with PitNETs who underwent endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery. ICG was intravenously injected before sellar floor drilling, then after the tumor-pituitary interface was fully exposed, real-time fusion mode fluorescence endoscopy was maintained for continuous observation. Two independent observers retrospectively assessed fluorescence intensity and contrast patterns on video clips of intraoperative fusion fluorescence imaging. Interobserver agreement for binary fluorescence intensity grading and three-category contrast pattern classification (tumor-dominant, equivalent, and pituitary-dominant) was evaluated using Cohen's kappa coefficient (weighted kappa for ordinal pattern categories). Surgery under fluorescence guidance was successfully completed for all 26 patients, with no ICG-related adverse events. No intraoperative mode switching was required, and fluorescence signals remained stable within the delay window. The contrast pattern classifications were: tumor-dominant n = 8 (all clinically functioning PRL-PitNETs), equivalent n = 15 (multiple subtypes), and pituitary-dominant n = 3 (all elderly patients ≥65 years with non-functioning PitNETs). Interobserver agreement was excellent, with Cohen's kappa of 0.91 (95% CI: 0.85-0.97, P < 0.001) for binary fluorescence intensity grading and a weighted Cohen's kappa of 0.89 (95% CI: 0.82-0.96, P < 0.001) for contrast pattern classification. All postoperative adverse events were mild and resolved conservatively, with no permanent pituitary dysfunction. Second-generation ICG fusion fluorescence endoscopy demonstrated preliminary technical feasibility and short-term safety for integration into transsphenoidal surgical workflow. The three fluorescence contrast patterns within the 15-18 min window show good interobserver agreement. The clinical utility of these patterns for tumor-pituitary interface assessment remains unproven and requires prospective validation.

papers.title: Two case reports of small cell lung cancer: typical CT manifestations, with one case illustrating adjunctive CT-based diagnosis without pathological confirmation.
papers.abstract: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a highly malignant neuroendocrine tumor with rapid progression and poor prognosis. Pathological examination is the gold standard for its diagnosis, yet pathological sampling is unfeasible in some clinical scenarios due to various constraints, making imaging and tumor markers critical for clinical decision-making. This two-case report describes the typical computed tomography (CT) findings of SCLC and explores the clinical value of combining CT imaging with tumor markers in guiding the diagnosis and treatment of SCLC patients for whom pathological confirmation is not feasible. We report two SCLC cases: Case 1 was a 56-year-old male with pathologically confirmed SCLC who presented typical imaging findings of hilar and mediastinal fused lymph nodes and achieved a partial response after combined chemoradiotherapy. Case 2 was a 67-year-old male with chest tightness and hemoptysis for 2 months, whose chest CT showed fused lymph nodes (a typical SCLC feature) and markedly elevated neuron-specific enolase (NSE: 221 ng/mL; reference range 1-16.2 ng/mL). Biopsy was unfeasible due to recent coronary stenting and ongoing antiplatelet therapy, and a clinical diagnosis of limited-stage SCLC was made via a combination of typical CT imaging features, significantly elevated NSE and clinical symptoms. The patient received timely EC regimen chemotherapy and subsequent standard chemoradiotherapy, which resulted in a clinical complete response (CR). This case report details the typical CT manifestations of SCLC and demonstrates that the combined application of typical CT findings, tumor markers and clinical symptoms may provide a pragmatic basis for timely clinical diagnosis and treatment of SCLC patients when pathological sampling is not achievable. This approach may help avoid treatment delay and improve clinical outcomes for such patients, while emphasizing that pathological examination remains the gold standard for SCLC diagnosis.

papers.title: Pneumovesicoscopic en bloc resection of multifocal bladder paraganglioma: a case report.
papers.abstract: Bladder paraganglioma is a rare non-epithelial neuroendocrine tumor. Catecholamine release may cause micturition-related headache, palpitations, sweating, paroxysmal hypertension, or syncope, but cases without typical symptoms can be difficult to recognize before surgery. Complete surgical excision remains the mainstay of treatment. A 75-year-old woman was admitted after two bladder lesions were detected. She had no hematuria, lower urinary tract symptoms, or micturition-related headache, palpitations, sweating, or paroxysmal hypertension. Contrast-enhanced CT showed two hypervascular nodules near the bladder neck and on the left posterior wall, measuring 12 × 14 mm and 6 × 9 mm, respectively. Twenty-four-hour urinary free catecholamines were within the reference ranges. Plasma free normetanephrine was mildly elevated at 0.96 nmol/L (upper reference limit, 0.71 nmol/L; approximately 1.35 × ULN) when measured by LC-MS/MS under standardized sampling conditions, whereas plasma metanephrine and 3-methoxytyramine remained within their reference ranges. This profile was considered consistent with a clinically silent but mildly biochemically functional tumor. The patient underwent pneumovesicoscopic en bloc resection. Histopathology confirmed multifocal bladder paraganglioma confined to the submucosa, with negative surgical margins, a Ki-67 proliferation index <1%, and retained SDHB expression. Recovery was uneventful, and cystoscopy showed no recurrence at 12 months. Bladder paraganglioma should be considered in a hypervascular submucosal bladder mass with intact overlying mucosa even when typical catecholamine-related symptoms are absent. This single case supports the technical feasibility of pneumovesicoscopic en bloc resection for selected localized lesions, but the 12-month follow-up is insufficient to establish comparative effectiveness or long-term oncologic safety.

papers.title: Dexmedetomidine with transition to oral clonidine for stabilization of refractory agitation: A case report.
papers.abstract: Refractory delirium and agitation in advanced cancer are challenging to manage, particularly when patients have longer prognoses and goals that extend beyond end-of-life sedation. Dexmedetomidine, a highly selective α2-adrenergic agonist, has shown promise for managing refractory symptoms in palliative care. Dexmedetomidine may control agitation while preserving arousability, but prolonged intravenous use limits feasibility. To describe the use of dexmedetomidine as a stabilizing bridge rather than terminal sedation and transition to oral clonidine to facilitate discharge home in a patient with advanced cancer and a longer prognosis. A 45-year-old man with metastatic medullary thyroid carcinoma was admitted to the palliative care unit with severe opioid-refractory pain complicated by delirium and agitation, preventing initiation of palliative radiation. A dexmedetomidine infusion was titrated to 0.6 µg/kg/hr. To facilitate discharge home, we implemented a gradual cross-taper to oral clonidine (0.1 mg three times a day titrated to 0.5 mg four times a day) over 1 week while tapering dexmedetomidine by 0.1-0.2 µg/kg/hr decrements. The dexmedetomidine infusion rapidly achieved symptom control while preserving wakefulness and enabled diagnostic reassessment and completion of radiation therapy. The patient tolerated the transition to oral clonidine without recurrence of agitation or hemodynamic instability, was successfully discharged home, and remained clinically stable 5 months later. Dexmedetomidine may function as a stabilizing bridge rather than terminal sedation in selected palliative care patients with longer prognoses. Transition to oral clonidine can facilitate discontinuation of intravenous therapy and support outpatient symptom management. Prospective studies are needed to establish standardized transition protocols and identify optimal candidates for this strategy.

papers.title: CRISPR screens reveal MCT1-driven metabolic escape from SMAD3 inhibition as a therapeutic vulnerability.
papers.abstract: Resistance to therapy remains a critical challenge in cancer. This is exemplified by TGF-β pathway inhibitors which, despite broad clinical testing, have failed to deliver survival benefit. More precise SMAD3 targeting has shown preclinical promise, yet resistance mechanisms to SMAD3 inhibition remain entirely unknown. Using complementary genome-wide CRISPR activation and knockout screens, we discover that cancer cells escape SMAD3 inhibition through metabolic reprogramming. Strikingly, this escape is driven not by transcriptional bypass but by the lactate transporter MCT1, with the effect preserved across BRAF-mutated melanoma, KRAS-mutated lung adenocarcinoma, and mouse melanoma. Mechanistically, SMAD3 inhibition creates energetic stress that cancer cells exploit through MCT1. By conferring metabolic flexibility and switching toward glycolysis under drug pressure, MCT1 increases anabolic activity to drive lipid and cholesterol synthesis. Pharmacological and genetic MCT1 inhibition synergizes strongly with SMAD3 blockade to impair tumor viability in BRAF-mutated melanoma, while suppressing drug-tolerant cell emergence in BRAF inhibitor-resistant cells. Critically, this synergy extends to preclinical models, where co-inhibition of SMAD3 and MCT1 potently reduces tumor growth in vivo. Given the additional and well-established role of MCT1 in shaping the tumor immune microenvironment via lactate transport, these results position MCT1 as both a metabolic and immunological target and provide a strong rationale for the repurposing of TGF-β/SMAD3 pathway inhibitors in combination.

papers.title: Cellular and spatial continuum of TAM functional states governs immune exclusion and dictates immune checkpoint resistance in melanoma.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy has transformed melanoma treatment, yet many patients either fail to respond or develop resistance after an initial response. The cellular and spatial determinants within the tumor microenvironment (TME) that underlie these divergent ICI therapy outcomes remain poorly defined. Here, we aimed to characterize the immune composition and spatial organization of the TME associated with ICI response and resistance. We integrated public scRNA-seq data (N = 32) with in-house spatial transcriptomics and imaging mass cytometry from an independent melanoma cohort (N = 6) to achieve high-resolution spatial profiling of the TME. This multimodal approach allowed us to map cellular heterogeneity within discrete spatial neighborhoods. To validate our findings, we constructed a scRNA-seq derived signature-matrix and deconvoluted a bulk RNA-seq cohort (N = 334). Clinical associations were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox hazard models, and a machine-learning classifier. We identified a distinct tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) state, termed lipid-associated TAMs (LA-TAMs), characterized by conserved lipid metabolic programs and tumor-specific adaptations in glycolysis under hypoxic conditions. Deep spatial multi-omics profiling revealed divergent immune architectures associated with treatment outcomes. In non-responder patients, LA-TAMs colocalized with sparsely distributed TIM3⁺ exhausted CD8⁺ T cells within an immune-excluded TME. In contrast, responder patients harbored interferon-primed CCL4+ TAMs (IFN-TAMs) spatially associated with Granzyme B⁺ activated CD8⁺ T cells, reflecting an immune-active microenvironment. These findings define contrasting macrophage-centered immune neighborhoods linked to ICI response. Interestingly, patients with LA-TAM-enriched neighborhoods were consistently non-responders or progressed during follow-up, irrespective of the presence of IFN-TAM neighborhoods. Lastly, we constructed a single-cell-derived signature matrix that estimates TAM fractions from bulk RNA-seq data and revealed LA-TAM abundance as a robust, independent predictor of poor ICI response and survival in a validation cohort. Our study defines the spatial landscapes of TAM-heterogeneity in melanoma and identifies LA-TAM neighborhoods as an important feature of ICI resistance. Although patients span a continuum of TAM-centered immune states, the presence of LA-TAM is likely to diminish the beneficial effects of IFN-TAM-associated immune activation. Finally, our proposed Melanoma-TME-derived signature-matrix provides a translatable framework to robustly predict ICI response and resistance.

papers.title: Neoadjuvant pepinemab in combination with nivolumab and/or ipilimumab in resectable metastatic melanoma: a pilot biomarker-driven trial.
papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve event-free survival in metastatic melanoma, yet resistance and recurrence remain common. Here we evaluated pepinemab, a Semaphorin 4D (SEMA4D)-blocking antibody, in combination with anti-PD1 nivolumab and/or anti-CTLA4 ipilimumab in a pilot biomarker-driven neoadjuvant trial (NCT03769155) for patients with resectable metastatic melanoma. The primary endpoint was to determine if pepinemab combined with ICIs modulates phenotypic properties within the tumor microenvironment in a manner that enhances T effector cell infiltration. Secondary endpoints included safety and tolerability, pathological response rates and radiographical response. Patients received two neoadjuvant doses followed by curative-intent surgery and one year of adjuvant nivolumab. Pepinemab-containing regimens demonstrated manageable toxicity profiles and did not delay or preclude curative-intent surgical resection in the 38 patients treated. The trial met its primary endpoint, as enrichment of transcripts associated with activated dendritic cells and immune recruitment pathways was observed in tumors from patients receiving pepinemab-containing regimens. Further, immune remodeling was evident by formation of mature lymphoid aggregates resembling tertiary lymphoid structures that contained clonally expanded T cell receptor repertoires. While this study was not powered to assess clinical efficacy, our findings do support further evaluation of SEMA4D blockade as a strategy to modulate the tumor microenvironment and potentially augment immunotherapy in melanoma and other solid malignancies.

papers.title: Receptor-PET and 2-deoxy-2-[18F]fluoro-d-glucose Concordance-discordance and Flip-flop Phenomenon: Its Implications for Theranostics and Therapeutic Decision-making.
papers.abstract: With the development and expansion of new targeted radiotracers in Theranostics, defining the specific clinical indications for FDG-PET/CT is pivotal to personalised medicine and precision oncology. The "flip-flop" phenomenon refers to the reciprocal yet complementary relationship between lineage-specific receptor PET tracers and FDG PET/CT. However, in real-world scenarios, varying degrees of concordance between receptor-targeted PET and FDG-PET reflect a continuum rather than a binary classification. The concept of dual-tracer/multi-tracer PET, employed in neuroendocrine tumours and castration-resistant prostate cancer, is likely to influence treatment decision-making in other malignancies as well.

papers.title: Critical Role of Novel PET-Computed Tomography/MR Imaging-Based Quantitative Techniques in Assessing Efficacy of Theranostics.
papers.abstract: Theranostics pairs a molecularly targeted diagnostic imaging agent with its therapeutic counterpart, enabling personalized, molecularly guided therapy. Although 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography is not itself a theranostic radiopharmaceutical, it complements the theranostic workflow from patient selection and treatment planning of primary and metastatic sites to quantitative response assessment. This article reviews novel PET-computed tomography/MR imaging-based quantitative techniques for assessing theranostic efficacy, including volumetric and global disease burden metrics, kinetic modeling, and multimodality integration, with applications in thoracic malignancies, metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, and neuroendocrine tumors.

papers.title: Distinct proteomic and acylproteomic adaptations to succinate dehydrogenase loss in two cell contexts.
papers.abstract: The tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle and electron transport chain (ETC) are key metabolic pathways required for cellular ATP production. Though loss of these components impairs cell survival, such defects can paradoxically promote tumorigenesis. One example is loss of succinate dehydrogenase (SDH), which functions in both the TCA cycle and as Complex II of the ETC. Mutations in SDH subunits can cause pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma (PPGL), rare hereditary neuroendocrine tumors of chromaffin cells in the adrenal gland and the nerve ganglia. Why tumor formation upon SDH loss is limited to certain tissues remains unclear. We hypothesized that the metabolic and proteomic perturbations resulting from SDH loss are cell-type specific, favoring survival of chromaffin cells. We comprehensively examined the proteomic, acetylproteomic, and succinylproteomic effects of SDH loss in two cell models, immortalized mouse chromaffin cells (imCCs) and immortalized mouse embryonic fibroblasts (iMEFs). Perturbations in metabolite levels were determined by mass spectrometry. Effects of SDH loss on fatty acid β-oxidation (FAO) were assessed by stable isotope tracing and pharmacologic inhibition. SDH-loss imCCs show significant upregulation of mitochondrial proteins, including TCA cycle and FAO enzymes, with pronounced downregulation of nuclear proteins. Both imCCs and iMEFs demonstrate significant energy deficiency upon SDH loss, but FAO activity is uniquely increased in SDH-loss imCCs. While SDH loss increases both lysine-reactive acetyl-CoA and succinyl-CoA, SDH-loss imCCs and iMEFs show disproportionate hyperacetylation but mixed succinylation. Surprisingly, SDH-loss imCCs, but not iMEFs, display disproportionate hypoacetylation and hyposuccinylation of mitochondrial proteins.

papers.title: Pancreatic neuroendocrine carcinoma: Is surgical resection associated with improved overall survival?
International Initiative on a Refined Staging System for Medullary Thyroid Cancer: A Multinational Multicenter Study.
papers.abstract: To refine the suboptimal prognostic discrimination of the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) 8th edition TNM (TNM-8) staging system for medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). This retrospective study enrolled patients with MTC from 43 centers across 15 countries under the framework of the International Medullary Thyroid Cancer Staging Consortium (IMTCSC). Pooled data were analyzed with disease-specific survival as the primary end point. With M1 disease fixed in stage IVC, we redefined the schema for stages I to IVB in M0 patients. Using exhaustive enumeration, all possible TN combinations were fitted into multivariable Cox models, with the lowest Akaike information criterion (AIC) defining the proposed system. Prognostic discrimination was assessed using adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and the concordance index (C-index). The IMTCSC cohort included 2,573 patients with MTC (female-to-male ratio: 1.25; median age 52 years [IQR, 41-62]; median follow-up 76.3 months [IQR, 37.3-121.0]). Level VII metastasis correlated with poorer survival, supporting its upgrade to N1c. Exhaustive search of 116,284 admissible stage-grouping schemas identified the optimal model (lowest AIC) defining stages I to IVB: I (T1N0-N1a/T2N0), II (T1N1b/T2N1a/T3N0), III (T1N1c/T2N1b/T3N1a/T4aN0-N1a), IVA (T2N1c/T3N1b-N1c/T4aN1b), and IVB (T4aN1c/T4b any N). Compared with AJCC TNM-8 (stage I as reference; stage II aHR, 0.84, P = .652; stage III aHR, 1.48, P = .172; stage IV aHR, 7.95, P < .001), the proposed system showed a clearer monotonic increase in disease-specific death risk (stage II aHR 2.22; stage III aHR, 4.81; stage IV aHR 15.75; all P ≤ .001) and a higher C-index (0.892 v 0.856, P < .001), which was also evaluated in the SEER cohort (N = 1,909). The proposed MTC staging system confers an improved schema for prognostic stratification compared with AJCC TNM-8.
