papers.title: Squeezing Treatment-Induced Metabolic Alterations in Melanoma Cells Are Accompanied by Impaired Cluster of Differentiation 8-Positive T Cell and Natural Killer Cell Antitumor Effector Functions.
papers.abstract: The physical microenvironment of solid tumors exerts compressive forces on cancer cells, but how such mechanical stress contributes to melanoma immune evasion remains largely unknown. This study investigates whether compression-induced nuclear deformation and metabolic reprogramming facilitate immune escape and explores the regulatory role of microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (MITF). A three-dimensional (3D) melanoma spheroid model was established and subjected to microfluidic-based compressive stress. Nuclear morphology and cellular stiffness were evaluated using confocal microscopy and atomic force microscopy. Transcriptome sequencing and The Cancer Genome Atlas Skin Cutaneous Melanoma (TCGA-SKCM) transcriptomic analyses, together with differentially expressed gene (DEG) analysis, Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment, Seahorse metabolic assays, and flow cytometry, were used to identify key metabolic pathways and evaluate cluster of differentiation 8-positive (CD8+) T cell and natural killer (NK) cell function. MITF was silenced via lentiviral short hairpin RNA (shRNA) to determine its functional involvement. Squeezing (Sqz) treatment triggered marked nuclear elongation, reduced cellular stiffness, and enhanced both mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and glycolysis in melanoma cells. These metabolic alterations were accompanied by impaired interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma) and Granzyme B production in CD8+ T cells and reduced NK cell effector activity, together with increased immune cell apoptosis. Public TCGA-SKCM analyses further supported an association between high MITF expression, reduced cytotoxic immune signatures, lower immune infiltration, and MITF-related metabolic pathway enrichment. MITF knockdown attenuated nuclear deformation, suppressed metabolic overactivation, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, and rescued CD8+ T cell- and NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity. Sqz-induced metabolic alterations in melanoma cells are accompanied by impaired CD8+ T cell and NK cell antitumor effector functions. MITF may act as an important molecular link connecting nuclear mechanotransduction, metabolic reprogramming, and immune escape, suggesting a potential strategy for counteracting physical stress-driven immunosuppression.

papers.title: Management of Obesity in Special Populations and Limited-Resource Settings: An Egyptian Medical Position Statement.
papers.abstract: Obesity/adiposity-based chronic disease is a chronic progressive relapsing disease linked to several comorbidities, with rising prevalence in Egypt. Limited local guidelines and healthcare challenges necessitate evidence-based, culturally adapted strategies. The Egyptian Medical Association for the Study of Obesity convened a clinical multidisciplinary panel to develop consensus recommendations. Evidence was synthesized from literature, prioritizing resource-limited settings and special situations. Assessment: Move beyond Body Mass Index to include waist circumference, waist/height ratio, body composition, and screening for obesity-related complications and diseases. Lifestyle Interventions: a-Nutrition: Mediterranean/dietary approach to stop hypertension diets, slow eating, and supervised fasting (eg Ramadan and Christian). b-Activity: Culturally tailored approaches (eg prayer-time movement and Arabic apps). c-Behavior: Cognitive-behavioral therapy and family-inclusive support. Pharmacotherapy: Use of approved agents (orlistat, naltrexone/bupropion, liraglutide, semaglutide, and tirzepatide) according to obesity-related complications and diseases and age group. Avoid GLP-1, GLP-1/GIP analogues in patients with medullary thyroid cancer, and all agents during pregnancy. Bariatric Surgery: Indicated for body mass index ≥40 kg/m2 (or ≥35 with obesity-related complications and diseases), with lifelong micronutrient supplementation. Special Populations: a-Adolescents: Focus on growth, not only weight-loss; consider pharmacotherapy in different age groups. b-Elderly: Prioritize muscle preservation; avoid weight loss unless obesity-related complications and diseases exist. c-Pregnancy: No weight loss; delay postpartum interventions until lactation is established. Policy Actions: Mandate food labeling, tax sugar-sweetened beverages, and integrate obesity services into primary healthcare. These recommendations provide a pragmatic framework for obesity/adiposity-based chronic disease management in Egypt, emphasizing affordable, patient-centered care, and clinical multidisciplinary collaboration and policy support.
papers.journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy

papers.title: Exploring the potential role of PD-L2 in primary melanoma immunotherapy resistance: a hypothesis-driven dual-ligand framework.
papers.abstract: The treatment of melanoma has been significantly improved by immune checkpoint blockade (ICB); however, primary immune resistance, particularly in PD-L1-negative tumors and in selected treatment contexts, remains a critical efficacy bottleneck. Traditional biomarkers show clear limitations in explaining resistance mechanisms and guiding clinical stratification. This review systematically proposes and elucidates the dual-ligand resistance model, comprehensively examines the molecular structure of programmed death-ligand 2 (PD-L2), its distinct dual-receptor interaction pattern with programmed death-1 (PD-1) and repulsive guidance molecule b (RGMb), and its multi-layered regulatory network, and explores the potential clinical value of PD-L2 as a context-dependent biomarker for primary immune resistance in melanoma and a potential therapeutic target. Within this framework, PD-L2 may contribute to immune escape in selected contexts, particularly in PD-L1-negative tumors or after PD-L1-targeted therapy. The expression of PD-L2 is regulated by genomic, epigenetic, microenvironmental, and host factors, with evidence of subtype-specific patterns. Available data suggest that PD-L2 may provide complementary biomarker value, although supporting evidence remains heterogeneous and prospective validation is limited. Targeting the PD-L2/RGMb axis has shown potential to reverse primary resistance in preclinical models, supporting further investigation. This synthesis positions PD-L2 as a candidate compensatory checkpoint in primary immune resistance in melanoma within a proposed dual-ligand resistance framework. However, its role should be interpreted as context dependent rather than universal. Further melanoma-specific and clinically validated studies are needed to define its biomarker and therapeutic value.

papers.title: Isolated Recurrent Syncope as the Initial Presentation of Pheochromocytoma: A Case Report of a Hidden Catecholamine-Secreting Tumor.
papers.abstract: Syncope is a common clinical presentation, yet a substantial proportion of cases remain unexplained despite guideline-directed evaluation. Pheochromocytoma, although a well-recognized catecholamine-secreting tumor, rarely presents with syncope, particularly in the absence of classical adrenergic symptoms, leading to diagnostic delay. We report a 60-year-old previously healthy female with recurrent episodes of transient loss of consciousness over two months, characterized by abrupt onset, brief duration, and complete spontaneous recovery without prodromal or postictal features. Despite repeated emergency presentations and an extensive negative workup including serial electrocardiograms, continuous cardiac monitoring, transthoracic echocardiography, orthostatic testing, tilt-table testing, carotid sinus massage, neurological evaluation, brain imaging, and laboratory studies, no cause was identified. Electrocardiography was normal and D-dimer testing excluded pulmonary embolism. Diagnosis was ultimately suggested by physical examination revealing a right flank mass, with abdominal computed tomography demonstrating a 5.6 cm adrenal lesion and biochemical testing confirming markedly elevated plasma free metanephrine (3.8 nmol/L; reference <0.50 nmol/L) and normetanephrine (9.6 nmol/L; reference <0.90 nmol/L), consistent with pheochromocytoma. Following appropriate preoperative preparation and surgical resection, the patient experienced complete resolution of syncope. This case highlights pheochromocytoma as a rare but reversible cause of recurrent unexplained syncope and underscores a potential diagnostic limitation of standard syncope workup, where intermittent catecholamine surges may evade detection, reinforcing the continued value of thorough physical examination in refractory cases.

papers.title: The Current Role of Blue Laser in Otologic Surgery: A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Blue laser technology, specifically the 445-450 nm wavelength blue diode laser, represents an emerging innovation in otologic surgery with unique photoangiolytic and hemostatic properties. This narrative review discusses evidence from otologic studies directly addressing the 445-450 nm blue diode laser to evaluate the clinical applications, outcomes, and safety profile of blue laser systems in ear surgery. The technology has been explored in stapedotomy procedures for otosclerosis, middle ear paraganglioma excision, and cholesteatoma surgery. Preliminary and still limited clinical data suggest audiological outcomes broadly comparable to traditional carbon dioxide laser systems, with a proposed advantage in hemostasis and thermal. Direct otologic evidence remains limited to a small number of case series and retrospective comparisons, with most publications emerging between 2018 and 2025. This review identifies blue laser technology as a promising adjunct to the otologic surgeon's armamentarium, warranting larger randomized controlled trials to establish definitive clinical guidelines and long-term safety profiles.
papers.journal: The journal of international advanced otology

papers.title: Cytopathologist Navigating Familial Thyroid Tumor Syndromes: From Fine-Needle Aspiration to Genetic Referral.
papers.abstract: Thyroid fine-needle aspiration (FNA) is primarily a lesion-specific diagnostic test; however, when cytomorphologic findings are interpreted alongside clinical and ultrasound features, they may provide important clues to an underlying hereditary thyroid tumor syndrome. Although familial syndromes are rarely diagnosed by cytology alone, cytopathologists play a pivotal role in recognizing patterns that warrant broader evaluation. Suspicion increases when cytologic findings correlate with young patient age, multifocal or multinodular disease, associated syndromic manifestations, or distinctive ultrasound appearances, prompting ancillary studies, targeted reporting, and consideration of genetic counseling or germline testing. Medullary thyroid carcinoma remains the clearest example of this integrated approach. Its characteristic cytomorphology, supported by calcitonin-based ancillary testing, can strongly suggest the diagnosis, whereas germline RET analysis is required to distinguish hereditary from sporadic disease. Cribriform-morular thyroid carcinoma is another important sentinel lesion, as its WNT/β-catenin-driven morphology should raise suspicion for APC-associated familial adenomatous polyposis, despite the recognized occurrence of sporadic APC- or CTNNB1-altered tumors. In contrast, DICER1-associated thyroid disease, PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome, and nonsyndromic familial nonmedullary thyroid carcinoma lack pathognomonic FNA features. Nevertheless, subtle distinctions may aid recognition. In particular, papillary architectural features occurring with macrofollicular structures may suggest a DICER1-associated lesion. Overall, these observations support a practical framework in which ultrasound findings, cytomorphology, and genetic considerations are interpreted as a unified diagnostic triad. This model clarifies what thyroid cytology can diagnose, what it may reasonably suggest, and what requires further clinical, molecular, and genetic correlation to identify hereditary thyroid neoplasia and optimize patient management and guide appropriate surveillance.

papers.title: Catatonic signs during delirium in leptomeningeal melanoma: Treatment trade-offs in end-of-life care.
papers.abstract: Catatonic and delirious signs overlap, creating treatment dilemmas when sedation obscures diagnostic assessment. We describe serial assessment and medication decision-making in advanced leptomeningeal melanoma during transition to home hospice. Inpatient observations, investigations, medication exposures, goals-of-care discussions, and serial Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale (BFCRS) examinations were synthesized. A man in his late 30s with metastatic melanoma involving the leptomeninges and brain developed fluctuating arousal, inattention, disorientation, mutism, immobility, staring, withdrawal, and waxy flexibility. His Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale (BFCRS) score decreased from 7 to 1 after intravenous lorazepam, although reassessment was limited by sedation and fluctuating wakefulness. Transient improvements in movement and speech did not translate into sustained gains in attention, communication, intake, mobility, or function. Lorazepam was subsequently reduced and discontinued when severe agitation emerged. As catatonic signs became less sustained and agitation threatened safety, scheduled haloperidol was introduced, with improvement in evening agitation and no documented extrapyramidal symptoms, oversedation, or QTc prolongation. A supervised oral-medication trial supported discharge planning, although hospice placement remained delayed by insurance barriers. A lower BFCRS score after lorazepam does not necessarily indicate meaningful clinical response if arousal, attention, and function remain impaired. In advanced cancer, catatonic signs may occur within a broader delirious or toxic-neurologic encephalopathy. Serial assessment should therefore incorporate wakefulness, attention, mobility, communication, and patient- and caregiver-defined goals. Treatment should be guided by the immediate priorities of interaction, safety, or comfort and continually reassessed in light of prognosis and feasibility of home care.

papers.title: Multiple Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Postoperative Residual Tumor in Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors.
papers.abstract: To develop and validate an interpretable machine learning (ML) model for predicting radiologically confirmed postoperative residual tumor (RT) in pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs). We retrospectively analyzed 584 surgically treated patients with PitNETs from a single center, using a random 7:3 training-test split and internal cross-validation. The primary endpoint was radiologically confirmed postoperative RT, assessed using MRI obtained within 48 h after surgery and longitudinal follow-up MRI. Candidate variables were selected using LASSO regression, with nine ML algorithms developed. Discrimination, calibration, clinical utility, interobserver agreement, and SHAP-based interpretability were assessed. Postoperative RT occurred in 72 patients (12.3%). Sensitivity analysis showed high agreement between 48-h MRI and follow-up confirmation (96.4%; Cohen's kappa = 0.837). Interobserver agreement was high for retrosellar invasion (kappa = 0.825), internal carotid artery invasion (kappa = 0.960), and Knosp grade (quadratic weighted kappa = 0.994). Eight predictors were retained: maximum sagittal diameter, maximum coronal diameter, age, Knosp grade, internal carotid artery invasion, sphenoid sinus pneumatization, tumor consistency, and retrosellar invasion. In the internal test set, the random forest model achieved high discrimination (AUC = 0.945; accuracy = 0.938), with performance comparable to LightGBM and XGBoost in DeLong testing. LightGBM had the lowest Brier score. Random forest was selected for the web tool after internal evaluation, with discrimination comparable to LightGBM, XGBoost, and SVM. Its generalizability to other centers and future patient cohorts remains unproven because evaluation used only a single-center random split and internal cross-validation. External and temporal validation with calibration assessment is needed before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Prolonged and Nocturnal Hypoglycemia Following Resection of Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma: A Prospective Study Using Intermittent-Scanning Continuous Glucose Monitoring.
papers.abstract: To characterize the temporal dynamics and persistence of hypoglycemia following the resection of pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma using intermittent-scanning continuous glucose monitoring. Twenty-two patients who underwent resection of pheochromocytoma (n = 20) or paraganglioma (n = 2) were prospectively enrolled. Perioperative glucose levels were tracked using intermittent-scanning continuous glucose monitoring (FreeStyle Libre Pro, Abbott), alongside conventional arterial or capillary blood glucose measurement. The endpoints were the time below range, defined as the percentage of time with glucose levels < 70 mg/dL. Postoperative hypoglycemia was defined as blood glucose levels below 70 mg/dL or symptomatic events requiring glucose administration. Eleven patients (50%) experienced postoperative hypoglycemia, with a median onset of 180 min after resection. During a median observation period of 7 days, the mean time below range remained high, ranging from 22% to 37%. Notably, the nocturnal time below range (00:00-06:00) was elevated, reaching 36% to 55%. An increased 7-day time below range was significantly associated with postoperative hypoglycemia and female sex. The time below range from postoperative Day 5 onwards in patients who experienced early postoperative hypoglycemia remained significantly higher than in those without postoperative hypoglycemia. Perioperative hormonal analysis suggested that the rapid resolution of insulin resistance preceded the recovery of insulin secretion. This prospective study suggests that prolonged susceptibility to nocturnal glucose dips can persist after the resection of pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma. Patients who develop clinical postoperative hypoglycemia and female sex may serve as indicators for this prolonged susceptibility, suggesting a need for extended monitoring and intervention.
papers.journal: International journal of urology : official journal of the Japanese Urological Association

papers.title: Incremental value of delayed [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/MR in the detection of liver metastases from gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors.
papers.abstract: [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT has been widely used in the diagnosis and staging of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs), while PET/MR may have greater advantages in the diagnosis of hepatic lesions. This study aimed to compare the diagnostic performance of conventional [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT and delayed PET/MR in detecting hepatic metastases in patients with GEP-NETs. This prospective observational study enrolled GEP-NETs patients with liver metastases who underwent conventional [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT followed by delayed PET/MR of the upper abdomen on the same day. The final status of all identified lesions was defined by a composite reference standard integrating histopathology, clinical follow-up, and contrast-enhanced MRI findings. Lesion detection rates, maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax), target-to-background ratio (TBR), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were compared between the two modalities. 46 patients (mean age 56.4 ± 12.9 years, 18 males and 28 females) were included. A total of 542 liver metastases were identified, with PET/CT detecting 368 (67.9%) lesions and delayed PET/MR contributing an additional 146 (94.8%) lesions. For matched lesions, SUVmax and TBR values showed no statistically significant differences between PET/CT and delayed PET/MR imaging (17.2 ± 11.0 vs. 16.4 ± 10.8, P = 0.746; 4.1 ± 3.6 vs. 4.0 ± 2.8, P = 0.178, respectively). For additional lesions detected on delayed PET/MR, 54 high-uptake liver metastases were identified (mean diameter 4.7 ± 1.9 mm; SUVmax 9.1 ± 2.2), along with 92 non-uptake lesions (mean diameter 5.5 ± 2.3 mm; Z = - 2.149, P = 0.0315). The sensitivity, specificity and accuracy between conventional PET/CT and delayed PET/MR were (65.9% vs. 92.4%, P < 0.001), (59.3% vs. 51.9%, P = 0.77) and (65.6% vs.90.5%, P < 0.001), respectively. Delayed [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/MR with an optimized acquisition protocol improved liver metastasis detection in GEP-NETs compared with conventional PET/CT. Combining PET/CT with delayed PET/MR provides a complementary strategy for hepatic staging in selected clinical settings.

papers.title: Primary ovarian insular carcinoid in an infertile woman managed with fertility preservation: a case report.
papers.abstract: Primary ovarian carcinoid tumors are uncommon neuroendocrine neoplasms, most often arising within mature cystic teratomas. Preoperative diagnosis is difficult because their imaging features may overlap with those of malignant epithelial ovarian tumors. Management is particularly challenging in young patients who desire fertility preservation, as evidence is limited and largely based on case reports. We report a 30-year-old nulligravid woman with a two-year history of primary infertility who presented with intermittent pelvic pain, menorrhagia, and a persistent enlarging right ovarian mass. Her ovarian reserve was favorable, and hysterosalpingography showed left proximal tubal obstruction with right tubal patency. Preoperative color Doppler transvaginal ultrasonography demonstrated a solid hypervascular right ovarian lesion classified as O-RADS 5, raising strong suspicion for malignancy. Primary laparotomy with staging was recommended, but the patient declined because of fertility-related concerns. She initially underwent laparoscopic right ovarian cystectomy/mass excision with preservation of the ovarian cortex. Frozen section suggested a neuroendocrine neoplasm. After final histopathological diagnosis and multidisciplinary review, embryo cryopreservation was performed, followed by definitive staging laparotomy including right oophorectomy, peritoneal washing cytology, omental biopsy, ipsilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy, and appendectomy. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry supported a well-differentiated primary ovarian insular carcinoid arising within a mature cystic teratoma, with findings most consistent with FIGO stage IA disease. Conventional postoperative imaging and gastrointestinal endoscopy did not identify an extragonadal primary tumor or metastasis. At 6 months, the patient remained disease-free. This case further illustrates that radiologically high-risk O-RADS 5 ovarian masses may ultimately represent rare, low-grade malignant neoplasms. Fertility-preserving management may be considered in carefully selected young patients after multidisciplinary evaluation, appropriate staging, and exclusion of metastatic disease. Longer follow-up is required before definitive oncologic conclusions can be made.

papers.title: Early Cause-Specific Mortality in Merkel Cell Carcinoma in the Immunotherapy Era.
Percutaneous and endovascular procedures in adrenal disease: indications, technique, and outcomes.
papers.abstract: Adrenal masses are found on roughly 4-5% of abdominal imaging studies, and the proportion rises with age. Most are benign, non-functioning adenomas that need imaging characterization and hormonal screening but no intervention. The remainder, comprising metastases, adrenocortical carcinoma, pheochromocytoma and hormonally active adenomas, raise questions that computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging cannot always settle; in these cases image-guided procedures can help. Percutaneous biopsy is reserved for hormonally inactive lesions whose benignity imaging has not established and whose histology would change management. Adrenal venous sampling remains the reference method for lateralizing aldosterone excess in primary aldosteronism and therefore decides who is offered adrenalectomy, although success depends heavily on operator experience and local protocol. Thermal ablation has produced biochemical and blood-pressure responses in selected aldosterone-producing adenomas and local control of limited metastases, but the evidence is largely nonrandomized and does not establish equivalence with surgery. Transarterial embolization serves three purposes: hemostasis in adrenal hemorrhage, devascularization before resection of hypervascular tumors, and functional treatment of aldosteronism, now supported by one small randomized trial. Each procedure carries hazards peculiar to the gland (catecholamine crisis, adrenal insufficiency after bilateral treatment, non-target embolization) that shape patient selection and periprocedural monitoring. This review covers indications, technique, outcomes and complications for each. Surgery remains the treatment of choice for most operable patients. Interventional radiology is most useful when the indications for sampling, ablation or embolization are recognized early and discussed at the multidisciplinary meeting, not only after surgery has been declined.

papers.title: Genetic testing considerations for hereditary duodenopancreatic neuroendocrine tumors.
papers.abstract: The incidence of duodenal and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (dpNETs) has increased substantially in recent years. These tumors may be due to syndromic hereditary predisposition syndromes: multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) or 4 (MEN4), Von Hippel-Lindau disease (VHL), neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), or tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC). Because a dpNET may be the first MEN1 sign, recent guidelines recommend MEN1 genetic testing in selected patients with an isolated dpNET. Whether similar genetic testing strategies should be extended to other hereditary syndromes remains unknown. We conducted a retrospective analysis of the genetic and clinical data of patients who underwent genetic testing for isolated or syndromic dpNETs. We assessed the presence of (likely) pathogenic variants ((L)PVs) in MEN1, NF1, VHL, CDKN1B, TSC1, and TSC2. 410 patients were included: 301 with isolated (=non syndromic) dpNETs and 109 with syndromic dpNETs. Among them, 38 carried a (L)PV, most frequently in MEN1 (n = 27 patients), followed by NF1 (n = 8) and VHL (n = 3). No TSC1, TSC2, or CDKN1B (L)PVs were found. Patients with syndromic dpNETs exhibited significantly higher positive rates (29.4%) compared to isolated dpNETs (<2%). We confirm that MEN1 is the predominant gene underlying predisposition to dpNETs. The low diagnostic yield in isolated dpNETs supports a clinically stratified genetic testing strategy. Clinical evaluation should systematically assess for signs of MEN1, MEN4, VHL, NF1, or TSC to inform appropriate genetic testing and maximize diagnostic yield. Concerning MEN1, we propose limiting extended genetic testing in patients with isolated dpNETs to those with (i) gastrinoma, (ii) multiple dpNETs, or (iii) diagnosis before 40 years of age.

papers.title: The gut microbiome in immunotherapy - lessons learned from melanoma and implications for gastrointestinal tumors.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has revolutionized the therapeutic landscape in both hematology and oncology. Critically, persistent remissions are achieved in up to 50 % of patients. As a result, there is an increasing demand for the identification of predictive biomarkers and novel therapeutic targets. Bacterial species of the gastrointestinal microbiome have been suggested to fill in that gap at an early time point. Critically, most studies have initially been conducted in patients suffering from tumor entities outside of the gastrointestinal tract, meaning that insights into the role of the gut microbiome in immunotherapy are mostly available for diseases such as metastatic malignant melanoma. Within this context, this narrative review summarizes four key lessons from immunotherapy research in melanoma and highlights their implications for the still-growing body of evidence on gastrointestinal cancers. Lessons learned from immunotherapy in malignant melanoma.

papers.title: Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms: Integrating WHO Classification with CT, MRI, and Molecular Imaging.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (pNENs) are a heterogeneous group of tumors within gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (GEP-NENs), with variable clinical behavior and prognosis. The World Health Organization (WHO) classification distinguishes well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) from poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs), including the recognition of grade 3 NETs (NET G3) as a separate entity with important clinical implications. Multiphasic computed tomography (CT) and multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are central to detection, staging, and follow-up, with MRI offering superior sensitivity for liver metastases, particularly with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and hepatobiliary phase (HBP). Molecular imaging with somatostatin receptor-targeted PET and 18F-FDG PET provides complementary biologic information by assessing receptor expression, metabolic aggressiveness, and tumor heterogeneity. SSTR-targeted PET supports confirmation of neuroendocrine phenotype, whole-body staging, and selection of candidates for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, whereas 18F-FDG PET identifies aggressive or dedifferentiated tumor components that may influence prognosis and favor chemotherapy-oriented strategies. Despite advances, noninvasive grading remains limited, requiring integration of imaging with histopathology. An integrated multimodality approach combining CT, MRI, molecular imaging, and pathology is therefore essential for accurate staging, biopsy targeting, treatment stratification, and personalized management.
papers.journal: Revista espanola de medicina nuclear e imagen molecular

papers.title: [Integration of molecular, genetic, and surgical evidence into the indication criteria for preventive thyroid surgery].
papers.abstract: Preventive thyroid surgery aims to prevent the occurrence of malignant diseases or improve their prognosis. The main indication is hereditary medullary thyroid carcinoma, which is caused by pathogenic RET germline variants. Other clinical manifestations can also occur in the context of multiple endocrine neoplasia. Early prophylactic thyroidectomy in the asymptomatic stage can make this tumour entity curable. The timing of surgery depends on the genotype and the associated risk classification and calcitonin levels, with particularly aggressive mutations requiring intervention as early as the first year of life.In contrast, the benefit of prophylactic lymph node dissection in papillary thyroid carcinoma remains controversial: While individual studies show a reduction in the recurrence rate, the risk of postoperative complications such as hypoparathyroidism or recurrent nerve palsy is increased. Therefore, the current guideline recommends an individualised approach with risk-adapted indications, taking into account tumour size, histology, and molecular markers.Although thyroid removal eliminates the risk of cancer, it requires lifelong hormone replacement therapy and close follow-up care. Extending the procedure to include prophylactic lymphadenectomy can increase morbidity.Future developments in molecular genetic diagnostics and refined risk stratification should help identify patients with high cancer risk even more precisely and, at the same time, avoid unnecessary interventions. Overall, preventive thyroid surgery is a successful example of personalised prevention, with indications that are becoming increasingly differentiated and patient-oriented.

papers.title: Epigenomic profiling suggests a common origin of both components in mixed gangliocytoma-pituitary neuroendocrine tumors.
papers.abstract: Mixed gangliocytoma-pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (GC-PitNETs) are rare pituitary tumors composed of neuroendocrine and gangliocytic elements. Recent studies have demonstrated shared features between neuroendocrine and gangliocytic cells. Specifically, co-expression of neuronal-associated cytoskeletal proteins and pituitary cell lineage transcription factors supports the hypothesis of a common origin of the cells in these tumors. In this multi-institutional study, we characterize the epigenomic profiles of a series of GC-PitNETs by DNA methylation analyses. Twenty-two cases, classified according to the 2022 WHO Classification, were studied including 13 somatotroph, 4 corticotroph, 4 mixed somatotroph-lactotroph, and 1 lactotroph GC-PitNETs. DNA methylation profiles of 21 tumors were analyzed using CNS tumor classifiers (Epignostix Heidelberg v12.8 and NCI Bethesda v 3.1), and unsupervised dimensionality reduction methods. The analysis revealed that all 21 evaluated GC-PitNETs exhibited epigenomic profiles aligning strictly with PitNET/adenoma classes matching their WHO histological diagnoses and showing no epigenomic affiliation with neuronal or glioneuronal reference tumors. These findings indicate that the gangliocytic component of GC-PitNETs lacks a distinct epigenomic signature, supporting the hypothesis that these cells may represent transdifferentiated neuroendocrine cells. Consequently, we propose reclassifying GC-PitNETs within tumors of the anterior pituitary neuroendocrine system and be renamed "pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (subtype) with gangliocytic differentiation."
papers.journal: Journal of neuropathology and experimental neurology

papers.title: ASO Visual Abstract: The Use and Utility of Preoperative Somatostatin Receptor-based Imaging in Gastroenteropancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors.
Pre-treatment machine learning prediction of local failure and time to local failure after Gamma Knife radiosurgery for radioresistant brain metastases.
papers.abstract: Local control after Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for radioresistant brain metastases remains variable. Melanoma and renal cell carcinoma brain metastases are relatively radioresistant, yet pre-treatment prediction of local failure and its timing remains limited. We developed and internally validated a survival machine learning model to predict lesion-specific local failure and time to local failure using only pre-GKRS variables. We performed a retrospective single-center study of melanoma and renal cell carcinoma brain metastases treated with GKRS. Local failure was modeled as a right-censored survival outcome. A Random Survival Forest (RSF) was trained using baseline demographic, clinical, and tumor-level variables available before treatment. The individual lesion was the prediction unit, while data partitioning was performed at the patient level to minimize information leakage. Performance was assessed using the concordance index, cumulative/dynamic AUC, and Brier score with patient-grouped 5-fold internal cross-validation. The cohort included 893 lesions, of which 228 (25.5%) developed local failure. In the holdout test set (179 lesions), the RSF achieved a C-index of 0.842. Dynamic AUC values were 0.904, 0.890, and 0.851 at 6, 12, and 24 months, respectively, with corresponding Brier scores of 0.130, 0.153, and 0.152. Cross-validation demonstrated stable performance, with a mean C-index of 0.882. The strongest predictors were age at treatment, pre-treatment KPS, and tumor volume. Pre-treatment RSF modeling demonstrated strong internal performance for predicting local failure and time to local failure after GKRS in radioresistant brain metastases, supporting its potential for individualized risk stratification and follow-up planning. Not applicable.

papers.title: PET Imaging of Dual GLP-1R and GIPR Targeting with [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-Tirzepatide.
papers.abstract: Tirzepatide is a clinical dual GLP-1R and GIPR agonist for type 2 diabetes and obesity, and non-invasive approaches to assess its in vivo biodistribution and systemic toxicity in living animals remain limited. Both receptors also serve as potential targets for neuroendocrine tumor imaging, and dual-target PET probes for simultaneous GLP-1R and GIPR detection are still lacking. Herein, we developed a novel PET probe [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-tirzepatide via structural modification of tirzepatide. This probe successfully visualized the in vivo distribution of tirzepatide, which was primarily eliminated through the renal system. The C20 fatty diacid moiety caused elevated uptake in the heart, liver and blood due to enhanced albumin binding. In vitro assays verified its reliable GLP-1R and moderate GIPR binding affinity. Persistent tumor accumulation was observed in INS-1 and A549-GIPR xenografts, allowing effective tumor visualization. In summary, [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-tirzepatide features facile radiolabeling and enables the clear visualization of tirzepatide in vivo, along with favorable dual-targeting performance, while excessive non-target uptake still needs to be optimized for further clinical translation.

papers.title: Novel [67Cu]Cu-Labeled 4-p-(Tolyl)butyric Acid-Conjugated Lactam-Cyclized Alpha-Melanocyte-Stimulating Hormone Peptides with Glycine and Polyethylene Glycol Linkers for Melanoma Targeting.
papers.abstract: This study managed to examine how the 4-p-(tolyl)butyric acid (p-TBA) albumin binder and the aspartic acid linker affect the tumor targeting and biodistribution properties of [67Cu]Cu-labeled p-TBA-conjugated alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) peptides. p-TBA was attached to 1,4,7-triazacyclononane-1,4,7-triacetic acid (NOTA)-Lys-Gly-Gly-Nle-c[Asp-His-DPhe-Arg-Trp-Lys]-CONH2 (NOTA-Lys-GGNle-CycMSHhex) and NOTA-Lys-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex with or without the Asp linker to generate NOTA-Lys(p-TBA/Asp-p-TBA)-GGNle-CycMSHhex and NOTA-Lys(p-TBA/Asp-p-TBA)-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex. The melanocortin-1 receptor (MC1R) binding affinities of the designed peptides were determined on B16/F10 melanoma cells. The biodistribution properties of [67Cu]Cu-NOTA-Lys(p-TBA/Asp-p-TBA)-GGNle-CycMSHhex and [67Cu]Cu-NOTA-Lys(p-TBA/Asp-p-TBA)-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex were evaluated on B16/F10 melanoma-bearing C57BL/6 mice at 2 h post-injection to select a lead peptide. Then, the melanoma targeting and imaging properties of [67Cu]Cu-NOTA-Lys(Asp-p-TBA)-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex were determined on B16/F10 melanoma-bearing C57BL/6 mice. The IC50 values of NOTA-Lys(p-TBA/Asp-p-TBA)-GGNle-CycMSHhex and NOTA-Lys(p-TBA/Asp-p-TBA)-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex were 0.26 ± 0.04, 0.54 ± 0.03, 0.46 ± 0.08, and 0.32 ± 0.04 nM, respectively. [67Cu]Cu-NOTA-Lys(Asp-p-TBA)-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex was selected as a lead peptide due to its highest tumor/kidney and tumor/liver uptake ratios among the [67Cu]Cu-peptides at 2 h post-injection. The B16/F10 melanoma uptake of [67Cu]Cu-NOTA-Lys(Asp-p-TBA)-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex was 29.31 ± 3.22, 39.05 ± 1.38, 25.07 ± 2.03, and 11.77 ± 1.61% ID/g at 0.5, 2, 4, and 24 h post-injection, respectively. The B16/F10 melanoma lesions were clearly visualized by SPECT/CT using [67Cu]Cu-NOTA-Lys(Asp-p-TBA)-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex as an imaging probe at 2 h post-injection. The utilization of p-TBA as an albumin binder prolonged the blood circulation and enhanced the tumor uptake of [67Cu]Cu-Asp-p-TBA-PEG as compared to [67Cu]Cu-NOTA-PEG2Nle-CycMSHhex without an albumin-binding moiety. The Asp linker expedited the blood clearance of [67Cu]Cu-Asp-p-TBA-PEG as compared to [67Cu]Cu-p-TBA-PEG. The combination of p-TBA, Asp, and PEG linkers resulted in the highest tumor/blood, tumor/kidney, and tumor/liver uptake ratios of [67Cu]Cu-Asp-p-TBA-PEG among the designed [67Cu]Cu-labeled p-TBA-conjugated CycMSHhex peptides. The favorable tumor targeting and blood clearance properties of [67Cu]Cu-Asp-p-TBA-PEG underscore its potential for future melanoma therapy.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulation-Guided 124I/211At-Labeled Aromatic Amide Derivatives as a Potential Theranostic Pair for Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Targeted alpha therapy (TAT) based on 211At represents a highly promising therapeutic strategy for various cancers, yet the rational design of molecular structures remains challenging in practical translation. In this work, we proposed a molecular dynamics (MD) simulation-guided strategy for constructing 124I/211At-labeled aromatic amide derivatives as a potential theranostic pair for melanoma. The interaction process between melanin and a series of aromatic amide derivatives was first investigated via MD simulation, emphasizing that dimethylamino derivatives possessed superior binding ability. Furthermore, radioiodinated dimethylamino derivative [124I]Dm-5-IPLA was proven to have the best tumor-targeting capability and favorable pharmacokinetics via systematic experimental investigations including in vitro cell testing, in vivo PET imaging, and ex vivo biodistribution investigations. Its therapeutic analogue, [211At]Dm-5-APLA, accordingly exhibited effective tumor growth inhibition and satisfactory safety in the TAT of B16F10 tumor-bearing mice, indicating the potential of 124I/211At-labeled aromatic amide derivatives for melanoma theranostics.

papers.title: [Adaptive resistance in melanoma: Understanding and targeting Drug-Tolerant Persister Cells].
B cells and the therapeutic index of checkpoint blockade.
papers.abstract: Combined CTLA-4 and PD-1 blockade is effective in treating melanoma and additional cancers but frequently causes immune-related adverse events (irAEs). irAEs cause treatment disruption and discontinuation and remain difficult to manage clinically. In this issue, Dhodapkar and colleagues assessed data from a small randomized clinical trial testing rituximab-mediated B cell depletion in combined CTLA-4/PD-1 blockade-treated patients with advanced melanoma. Despite premature discontinuation of the trial due to a high rate of rituximab hypersensitivity, they report that preemptive B cell depletion was associated with fewer severe toxicities without evident loss of antitumor activity. These findings raise broader questions about the organization of checkpoint-induced autoimmunity, the emerging concept of immune reset, and the compartment-specific roles of B cells in antitumor immunity.

papers.title: Cell state programs offer a potential axis for classifying neuroendocrine tumors.
papers.abstract: Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs) arise from hormone-producing cells in the gut and pancreas. Despite increasing incidence of these tumors, therapeutic options remain limited. Well-differentiated GEP-NETs are classified by anatomic site, morphology, and proliferation indices, but this approach offers limited prognostic resolution among phenotypically similar tumors and constrains personalization of treatment decisions. In this issue of the JCI, Karam, Hoffman, and colleagues profiled 38 pancreatic and small-intestinal NETs using joint single-nucleus RNA and ATAC sequencing and projected the resulting malignant cell-associated programs onto matched spatial transcriptomes. Two conserved malignant states emerged: neuronal-like and secretory neuroendocrine. These states span a continuum in both organ sites, are enriched for largely different transcription factor motifs, and occupy distinct microenvironmental niches. Secretory program scores trended higher in metastatic disease and may carry prognostic value. Taken together, these data describe NET heterogeneity as a cell state axis linked to tissue architecture.

papers.title: Merkel Cell Polyomavirus-Negative Merkel Cell Carcinoma Presenting in the Parotid Gland: Precise Diagnosis and Complete Pathological Response to Nivolumab.
papers.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare and aggressive cutaneous neuroendocrine carcinoma that may present diagnostic challenges, particularly in Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV)-negative cases. Distinguishing MCC from other high-grade neuroendocrine carcinomas is critical because treatment strategies differ. We report a case of a 77-year-old Caucasian male with a history of multiple non-melanoma skin cancers who presented with rapidly enlarging left parotid and cervical lymph node masses with suspected osseous metastasis to the fourth cervical vertebra (C4). Fine needle aspiration of the parotid mass demonstrated high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma, positive for synaptophysin, focally and weakly positive for cytokeratin 20 (CK20), and negative for thyroid transcription factor 1 (TTF-1) and Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV) immunoreactivity. Initial molecular classification favored small cell carcinoma. However, additional mutational signature analysis demonstrated an ultraviolet (UV) mutational profile consistent with cutaneous origin, supporting MCPyV-negative Merkel cell carcinoma. The diagnosis was revised following multidisciplinary review, and planned treatment was changed from carboplatin-etoposide chemotherapy to three months of nivolumab, a programmed death-1 (PD-1) inhibitor. Surgical resection of the parotid gland demonstrated complete pathologic response with no residual viable carcinoma identified. At the two-year follow-up, the patient was doing well with no MCC recurrence or metastasis identified. This case highlights the diagnostic difficulty of MCPyV-negative MCC presenting in an extracutaneous location and mimicking small cell carcinoma. In diagnostically challenging MCCs, molecular profiling and UV mutational signature analysis may play a key role in establishing correct diagnosis and treatment.

papers.title: Immunogenetic Signature of the MICA-129 Val/Val Genotype Associated With Metastasis in Melanoma.
papers.abstract: MICA (major histocompatibility complex class I [MHC class I] chain-related protein A) is a stress-induced glycoprotein that functions as a ligand for the NKG2D (natural killer [NK] group 2 member D) receptor, expressed on NK cells and CD8+ T lymphocytes (cytotoxic T cells), playing a key role in tumor immune surveillance. In melanoma, modulation of this axis promotes tumor immune evasion. The functional MICA-129 polymorphism (methionine [Met]/valine [Val]) alters the binding affinity to NKG2D, thereby influencing the cytotoxic immune response. This study included patients with basal cell carcinoma (BCC) and melanoma (primary and metastatic). The Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Melanoma (FACT-M) questionnaire was administered, followed by MICA-129 genotyping using quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), measurement of soluble MICA (sMICA) by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), analysis of MICA and NKG2D expression on CD8+ T lymphocytes by flow cytometry, and assessment of inflammatory cytokines and angiogenic factors. A higher frequency of the Val/Val genotype was observed in metastatic melanoma, whereas serum sMICA levels did not differ among the groups. The Val variant was associated with reduced functional stability of the MICA-NKG2D axis, favoring tumor immune evasion. Primary melanoma exhibited a more pronounced inflammatory profile, whereas metastatic melanoma showed greater angiogenic activity, indicating a microenvironment conducive to tumor progression. These findings suggest that the MICA-129 Val/Val genotype may serve as a prognostic biomarker and support the MICA-NKG2D axis as a potential therapeutic target in melanoma.

papers.title: Elucidation of the antimelanogenic effects of linoleic acid- and α-linolenic acid-derived solutions on B16F10 melanoma cells.
papers.abstract: Linoleic acid (LA) and α-linolenic acid (α-LA) are essential fatty acids that serve as precursors to diverse lipid mediators. In this study, we investigated the antimelanogenic potential of oxidized lipid mixtures generated from LA and α-LA using soybean lipoxygenase under oxygen-rich conditions. Treatment of B16F10 melanoma cells with these mixtures markedly suppressed forskolin-induced melanin production without detectable cytotoxicity. Fractionation of the LA-derived solution revealed that a fraction enriched in hydroxylated derivatives, including 9,10,13-trihydroxy-11-octadecenoic acid (9,10,13-THODA) and 9,12,13-trihydroxy-10-octadecenoic acid (9,12,13-THODA), exhibited inhibitory activity; however, this activity was weaker than that of the original solution, and the two major THODAs alone showed no inhibitory activity. The inhibitory effects were not primarily mediated by the direct suppression of Tyrosinase enzymatic activity, as substantial inhibition was observed only at higher concentrations in vitro. Instead, the LA- and α-LA-derived solutions downregulated forskolin-induced Tyrosinase protein expression. These findings suggest that oxidized derivatives of LA and α-LA contain bioactive lipid species that suppress melanogenesis through the modulation of Tyrosinase expression, providing a potential basis for the development of novel functional lipid-based modulators of pigmentation.

papers.title: Possible Contribution of Consistent Epidermal Attenuation to the Pearly Appearance of Facial Basal Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) and intradermal nevus (IN) can be difficult to distinguish clinically, even with dermoscopy, because IN may exhibit dermoscopic features similar to those of BCC. In contrast, the pearly appearance characteristic of BCC is usually absent in IN and may serve as an important diagnostic clue. We hypothesized that attenuation of the overlying epidermis might contribute to this appearance by enhancing surface reflection and increasing the visibility of underlying dermal components. We retrospectively evaluated 27 non-ulcerated facial BCCs (25 nodular and 2 morpheaform) and compared them with facial INs (n = 19), malignant melanomas (MM; n = 6), Merkel cell carcinomas (MCC; n = 3), and mixed tumors (MT; n = 4). Epidermal thickness and hair follicle density were quantitatively assessed in lesional and adjacent normal skin. Dermal mucin deposition and collagen staining intensity were also evaluated. The lesional epidermis was thinner than the adjacent normal epidermis in all 27 BCCs. The lesional-to-normal epidermal thickness ratio was significantly lower in BCC than in IN. The lesional-to-normal hair follicle density ratio was also significantly lower in BCC than in IN. Superficial dermal mucin deposition was observed in all BCCs but not in the other tumor types, whereas the lesional-to-normal collagen staining intensity ratio was comparable between BCC and IN. A pearly appearance was observed in all 25 nodular BCCs but not in the two morpheaform BCCs despite epidermal attenuation. None of the other tumor types exhibited a pearly appearance, including MM lesions with epidermal attenuation. These findings demonstrate that epidermal attenuation is a consistent histopathological feature of non-ulcerated nodular BCC and raise the possibility that it contributes to the characteristic pearly appearance of nodular BCC. However, because epidermal attenuation was also observed in lesions without a pearly appearance, its actual contribution remains uncertain and requires further investigation.

papers.title: Hotspot mutations and tumour spectrum in von Hippel-Lindau syndrome: genotype-phenotype analysis of a large Chinese cohort.
papers.abstract: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) syndrome is a rare autosomal dominant multisystem tumour syndrome caused by germline VHL mutations. The traditional classification of VHL syndrome, which is largely based on pheochromocytoma penetrance, is insufficient for individualised surveillance and management. This study aimed to improve mutation-specific risk stratification and define genotype-phenotype correlations of recurrent hotspot mutations in a large Chinese cohort. This retrospective single-centre study included 674 patients with VHL disease from 283 unrelated families. Four recurrent hotspot mutation subtypes were analysed: codon 65 missense mutations, exon 2 deletion, c.481C > T, and c.224_226del. Kaplan-Meier analysis and univariate and multivariate Cox regression models were used to assess age-related tumour risks and survival outcomes. Codon 65 missense mutations were associated with a lower risk of retinal angioma and pheochromocytoma, indicating a relatively mild phenotype. Exon 2 deletion was characterised by a higher prevalence, earlier onset, and increased age-related risk of retinal angioma and worse renal cell carcinoma (RCC)-specific survival. Increased prevalences and age-related risks of central nervous system hemangioblastoma (CHB), RCC, and pancreatic cysts or tumours were associated with c.481C > T mutations. The c.224_226del subtype showed a distinct CHB-predominant phenotype, with higher CHB incidence, earlier onset, lower pancreatic lesion risk, and higher overall mortality. Recurrent hotspot VHL mutation subtypes were associated with distinct clinical phenotypes and prognostic patterns. Mutation subtype-based classification (covering 19.6% of patients with VHL syndrome) may provide more precise guidance for surveillance, clinical decision-making, and genetic counselling than traditional broad classification models.

papers.title: Synthetic lethal screens reveal p300/CBP as a vulnerability for GNAQ-driven uveal melanomas.
papers.abstract: Uveal melanoma is the most common intraocular cancer in adults, driven by activating mutations in GNAQ or GNA11, which encode the G proteins Gαq and Gα11. Currently, therapeutic options for uveal melanoma, particularly metastatic uveal melanoma, remain limited. Through an isogenic CRISPR screening approach, we identify EP300, which encodes the protein lysine acetyltransferase p300, as a top synthetic lethal vulnerability in the context of GNAQ mutation. Notably, CREBBP, which encodes the closely related paralogue CBP, also emerges among the top-ranked candidates. Mechanistically, we find that p300 and CBP support YAP-dependent transcription downstream of oncogenic Gαq in uveal melanoma through interactions with YAP at chromatin. These interactions enhance H3K27 acetylation at the promoters and putative enhancers of YAP target genes and promote the recruitment of RNA polymerase II and CDK9. Using multiple in vivo models representing clinically relevant stages of Gαq-mutant uveal melanoma, we find that p300 inhibition, by both genetic and pharmacological approaches, profoundly impairs tumor growth and metastasis. Taken together, this study establishes p300 as a potential therapeutic target for Gαq-driven uveal melanoma, which is dependent on unrestrained YAP signaling.

papers.title: Incidental Thyroid Neuroendocrine Carcinoma Revealing a Presumed Occult Gastrointestinal Malignancy.
papers.abstract: In rare cases, a thyroid mass may represent metastatic neuroendocrine disease rather than a primary thyroid malignancy. This case report describes a unique presentation of neuroendocrine carcinoma involving the thyroid with concurrent somatostatin receptor-positive gastrointestinal and mesenteric lesions of uncertain origin, providing insight into the diagnostic and management challenges of this disease. We present a 60-year-old male patient found to have an incidental 11 cm left thyroid mass with airway displacement on neck computed tomography (CT). A left thyroid lobectomy was performed, and surgical pathology confirmed neuroendocrine carcinoma. Immunohistochemical and molecular testing argued against medullary thyroid carcinoma, while site-of-origin markers created a diagnostic challenge with features suggestive of both pulmonary and non-pulmonary origin. Subsequent DOTATATE positron emission tomography (PET) scan demonstrated somatostatin receptor-avid lesions involving the duodenum and mesentery, raising the possibility of a gastrointestinal primary with metastatic spread to the thyroid. The discordance between the immunohistochemical profile and imaging findings highlights the diagnostic complexity of neuroendocrine tumors involving the thyroid and underscores the importance of comprehensive systemic evaluation, including functional imaging and site-of-origin immunohistochemistry, in the setting of atypical thyroid pathology. Prompt recognition of potential systemic neuroendocrine malignancy is essential for staging and therapeutic planning.

papers.title: Characterizing bone metastases and skeletal-related events in patients with well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms utilizing <sup>68</sup>Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography.
papers.abstract: Tumors of neuroendocrine origin are a heterogenous group of related neoplasms which can arise from anywhere in the body. Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) are categorized by site of origin, differentiation status and grade (Ki-67 expression and/or mitotic rate), with significant prognostic variability accordingly. Historically, the prevalence of bone metastasis is reported to be 6%-12% based on "first generation" (i.e., <sup>111</sup>Indium pentetreotide [Octreoscan®]) somatostatin receptor imaging (SSRI). We conducted a retrospective cohort study including patients with well-differentiated NENs to determine the clinical and imaging characteristics of osseous metastases when evaluated with higher-sensitivity <sup>68</sup>Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography (PET) scans, as well as determining fracture prevalence in selected sub-cohorts. We also developed a risk score analysis to assess risk of fracture in this cohort. Four hundred twenty-four patients were identified for inclusion. The median age was 61 years. Most patients were asymptomatic (64%), had sclerotic lesions (77%), Krenning 4 (71%), and had >3 sites (69%) of osseous disease. A high proportion of patients had osseous metastases at sites with high risk for fracture, including vertebra (82%), pelvis (63%), and peri-trochanteric femur (34%). Fifty-seven patients (13%) in the entire cohort suffered a fracture. Fracture prevalence was significantly lower in small bowel neuroendocrine tumors (NETs, 7%) and Grades 1 and 2 disease (8% and 9%, respectively), with higher prevalence in pancreatic NETs, paragangliomas/pheochromocytomas, lung carcinoid, and Grade 3 disease (≥20% for each; p-values <.05). Our study showed that the rate of osseous metastatic disease approximates 20% in well-differentiated NENs. Most bone metastases are asymptomatic and the risk of fracture is variable based on the primary site of disease and tumor grade. Our novel risk score analysis for fracture was designed to assist clinician decision making as to management of bone metastasis in this patient population.

papers.title: Optimizing the Therapeutic Index: Sequential Intraarterial-Intravenous PRRT with Personalized Volumetric-Adjusted Dosing.
papers.abstract: Patients with well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) frequently present with liver-dominant metastases, which significantly impact prognosis and limit curative options. Although standard intravenous peptide receptor radionuclide therapy with 177Lu-DOTATATE is effective, strategies to intensify the radiation dose to hepatic lesions are needed to improve outcomes. This prospective clinical trial investigated the feasibility, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy of a personalized treatment schedule combining intraarterial and intravenous administrations of 177Lu-DOTATATE. Methods: Ten consecutive adults with progressive, nonresectable, liver-dominant metastatic gastroenteropancreatic NETs expressing somatostatin receptors were enrolled. The treatment protocol comprised 4 cycles of 177Lu-DOTATATE administered every 2 mo (2 initial intraarterial cycles followed by 2 intravenous cycles). Intraarterial administration involved angiographically guided, selective catheterization of the hepatic arteries with volumetrically adjusted activity to maximize targeted delivery. Safety monitoring, radiation protection, and dosimetry comparisons between intraarterial and intravenous routes were performed. Results: The intraarterial administration procedure was feasible in 100% of patients. Radiation exposure to staff and patients remained within regulatory limits, with no contamination events. Dosimetry analysis indicated that intraarterial administration (cycle 1) delivered a greater than 3-fold higher radiation dose to liver metastases compared with the intravenous route (cycle 3), although interim response may have played a role. Furthermore, 68Ga-DOTATATE PET imaging revealed an 86% increase in median liver lesion uptake with intraarterial administration. The regimen was generally well-tolerated, with only 1 severe adverse event reported (low esophageal tear), which was not attributed to the administration route. Efficacy analysis showed partial response rates in 67% of patients at the first follow-up 3 mo after treatment completion, improving to 87% at the second follow-up (6 mo) in accordance with RECIST and volumetric criteria. Conclusion: The sequential administration of intraarterial followed by intravenous 177Lu-DOTATATE is a feasible and safe therapeutic strategy for liver-dominant metastatic NETs. The use of a personalized, volumetric-based approach provided higher uptake and absorbed doses in hepatic metastases, with high objective response rates and effectively maintained systemic coverage.

papers.title: Primary Hepatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms: Systematic Review and Expert Pathologist Reappraisal Using the WHO 6th Edition Framework.
papers.abstract: Primary hepatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (PHNENs) are exceedingly rare. Published evidence often lacks adequate clinicopathological support for a primary hepatic origin and uses inconsistent historical terminology. Previous reviews have pooled well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumours (NETs), poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs), and mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs), despite differences in biology, prognosis, and management. We systematically reviewed reported PHNENs using PRISMA-based screening and expert pathology reappraisal within the WHO 6th edition morphology-first framework. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science. Titles, abstracts, and full texts were screened according to predefined eligibility criteria; eligible articles underwent second-level expert assessment of pathology, including morphology (including NET G3 vs. NEC and MiNEN vs. amphicrine carcinoma), immunohistochemistry (expression of at least two NE markers), proliferation (Ki-67/mitotic activity), as well as clinical/imaging work-up to exclude metastases from extrahepatic primaries. Of the 67 potentially eligible studies submitted to expert pathology-based reappraisal, 28 studies (49.1%) were retained in the final dataset with 57 likely NEN cases (mainly case reports/small case series). Among the 57 cases, most were well-differentiated NETs (78.9%); NECs (8.8%), MiNENs (3.5%), and amphicrine carcinomas (1.8%) were less frequent. Some cases were high-grade NENs that could not be distinguished as well or poorly differentiated (7%). PHNEN literature is constrained by rarity, uncertainty of hepatic origin, and historical misclassification. Future studies and registries should report a minimum diagnostic dataset with standardised terminology according to the WHO 6th edition framework and in-depth clinical/imaging studies.

papers.title: Genomic Alterations in Pulmonary Carcinoid Tumors: A Targeted Analysis of Gene Rearrangements and Oncogenic Mutations.
papers.abstract:
Introduction

Pulmonary carcinoids (PCs) are rare, well-differentiated, neuroendocrine lung tumors with limited treatment options for advanced disease, underscoring the need for targeted therapies. PCs typically exhibit a low mutational burden. Although MEN1 and chromatin-modifier mutations are known contributors, potentially actionable alterations remain poorly characterized. To better define therapeutic opportunities, we evaluated oncogenic fusions and variants across 17 cancer-associated genes in a large retrospective PC cohort.

Methods

Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded primary tumors from Helsinki University Hospital (n = 119, collected between 1990 and 2020) were subjected to targeted RNA-based fusion and variant analysis using the Archer FusionPlex Lung v2 assay.

Results

The most frequent recurrent genetic rearrangements involved ALK (n = 5), BRAF (n = 3), FGFR2 (n = 3), and NTRK3 (n = 2), each featuring diverse fusion partners. Variant analysis identified BRAF, EGFR, FGFR1, and FGFR3 as the most frequently mutated genes, although only 2.2% (n = 4) of all detected variants were classified as oncogenic. Notably, 66.7% of all oncogenic or likely oncogenic variants occurred in BRAF and EGFR. Oncogenic variants were identified in ALK, BRAF, EGFR, and ERBB2. Although all FGFR1-3 variants were of uncertain significance, their frequency (34.1% of all detected variants), together with the three FGFR2 fusions, suggested that FGFR alterations may be biologically relevant in PCs.

Conclusion

Despite the typically muted genomic landscape of PCs, our study revealed a small yet therapeutically relevant subset of alterations. The findings further characterized the molecular profile of PCs and identified potentially actionable molecular subgroups. While these alterations were not associated with disease-specific survival or metastatic status, they support consideration of molecular profiling in selected patients with advanced disease.

papers.title: Hematologic Consequences of Radiopharmaceutical Therapy: From Clonal Hematopoiesis to Therapy-Related Myeloid Neoplasms.
papers.abstract: Radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) uses radionuclides linked to targeting ligands to bind tumor-associated receptors or antigens and deliver ionizing radiation to malignant cells. Approved agents include [<sup>177</sup>Lu]Lu-DOTATATE for gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, [<sup>177</sup>Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, and <sup>223</sup>Ra-dichloride for bone-predominant metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Accumulating evidence suggests that RPT may impose genotoxic stress on the hematopoietic system, resulting in prolonged cytopenias and, in some patients, therapy-related myeloid neoplasms (tMNs). This review synthesizes evidence regarding hematologic toxicities associated with [<sup>177</sup>Lu]Lu-based RPT, emphasizing mechanisms of marrow injury, limitations of dose-only frameworks, host susceptibility factors, and emerging strategies for risk stratification, monitoring, and mitigation. We propose an integrated radiogenomic framework in which hematologic toxicity and tMN risk after RPT may arise from interactions among prior genotoxic exposure, heterogeneous red marrow radiation delivery, host genomic susceptibility-including clonal hematopoiesis and germline predisposition-and baseline marrow reserve. As RPT moves into earlier lines of therapy and populations with a longer expected survival, anticipating hematologic consequences will be essential for safe and precise clinical implementation.

papers.title: Metachronous and Sporadic Bilateral Carotid Body Paraganglioma.
papers.abstract:
Purpose

The Authors' goal is to highlight the importance of early diagnosis and management of metachronous carotid body paraganglioma (CBP), analysing and discussing the main features of this rare tumor.

Methods

This study review the literature on a very particular topic, reporting the case of a patient with the rare evidence of a metachronous CBP in the left side of the neck, which onset and was surgically treated 26 years after the first contralateral presentation.

Results

After excision, the diagnosis of CBP was confirmed by histological and immunohistochemical examination of the surgical specimen. Transient dysphonia and dysphagia were observed after surgery, both recovered after 1 years. No cardiac anomalies were detected.

Conclusion

Paragangliomas are rare neuroendocrine neoplasms with an incidence of 2-8 X 1,000,000. Paragangliomas of the head and neck (HNP) originate mainly from the carotid body (60%) and in a few cases from the jugular bulb, the medial promontory of the middle ear (30%), the vagal nerve and the nodose ganglion (5-10 %). Bilateral CBP represents an extremely rare entity, accounting for approximately 5% of patients with CBP. Diagnostic imaging of CBP includes ultrasound, Computed Tomography (CT), Magnetic Resonance Images (MRI) and Angiography. The treatment of choice for CBP is its complete surgical removal. Early detection of symptoms referable to a new CBP is very important, because of the possibility, even after many years, of contralateral presentation of the same tumor. This, if operated at an early stage, decrease the risk of neurovascular complications.

papers.title: Cell Surface Expression and PET Imaging Establish DLL3 as a Clinically Actionable Target in Neuroblastoma.
papers.abstract: In adult neuroendocrine malignancies, including small cell lung cancer, Delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3) is a validated therapeutic target. DLL3 is expressed in neuroblastoma, a pediatric cancer of neuroendocrine origin, but subcellular localization is incompletely defined, limiting clinical translation of DLL3-targeted therapies for neuroblastoma. Methods: DLL3 expression and localization were evaluated in human neuroblastoma tumors and preclinical models using RNA sequencing, immunohistochemistry, and flow cytometry. To assess in vivo tumor accessibility, DLL3-targeted PET imaging with [89Zr]Zr-deferoxamine-SC16.56 was performed in patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models and in 4 patients with neuroblastoma. Results: DLL3 was broadly expressed across neuroblastoma tumor samples and preclinical models. Although immunohistochemistry demonstrated variable protein expression, flow cytometry revealed near-universal DLL3 cell surface localization across clinical samples and PDX models, including tumors with low expression by immunohistochemistry. DLL3-targeted PET imaging demonstrated tumor-specific uptake in PDX models and in 4 patients with relapsed neuroblastoma, confirming in vivo accessibility of DLL3. Conclusion: DLL3 overexpression in neuroblastoma is associated with targetable cell surface localization, supporting DLL3 as a clinically actionable target for imaging and therapeutic strategies.
