papers.title: Expression of nestin in cancer: a tissue microarray study involving 13,318 cancers from 148 tumor entities.
papers.abstract:
Background

Nestin (neuroepithelial stem cell protein) is a class VI intermediate filament protein which is transiently expressed in subsets of precursor cells of various tissues during development. Nestin expression can be reinduced in the adult during pathological situations.

Methods

To better comprehend the prevalence of nestin in different cancer types, nestin was analyzed by immunohistochemistry on tissue microarrays (TMAs) containing 17,285 samples from 148 different tumor types. Our antibody was validated using a second independent antibody on 76 different normal tissues, ensuring a broad range of proteins to be tested for cross-reactivity.

Results

Of 13,318 analyzable tumors, nestin staining was absent in 11,677 (87.7%), weak in 961 (7.2%), moderate in 360 (2.7%), and strong in 320 (2.4%) cases. Of 148 tumor categories, 119 showed nestin staining in at least one case, and 57 included at least one sample with strong positivity. Nestin positivity was most seen in tumors of the salivary glands (up to 100%), gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (93.8%), tumors of the peripheral nerves (up to 93.8%) and malignant melanomas (81.8%). High nestin expression was linked to high grade (p < 0.0001), estrogen (p = 0.0054), and progesterone receptor negativity (p = 0.0051), as well as a triple negative phenotype (p = 0.0028) in invasive breast cancer NST, in papillary as well as poor ISUP (p=0.0149), Fuhrman (p=0.0006) and Thoenes grades (p=0.0099) in clear cell renal cell carcinoma, invasive tumor growth in urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder (pTa vs. pT2-4; p < 0.0001), and advanced pT stage (p = 0.0477) in serous carcinoma of the ovary.

Conclusions

The data from this study provide an overview of nestin expression in human cancer and demonstrate that increased nestin levels can occur in many different tumor entities. Significant associations with unfavorable tumor characteristics in multiple entities argue for a role of nestin in driving cancer aggressiveness, which may further support the concept of exploring nestin as a drug target.

papers.title: Non-small cell lung carcinoma and its mimics on cytology and small biopsy samples: a practical approach aligned with the WHO Reporting System.
papers.abstract: Accurate classification of lung tumors in cytology specimens and small biopsies remains a diagnostic challenge because of limited cellularity, preanalytical variables, and significant morphologic overlap among entities. This review summarizes key cytomorphologic characteristics and practical immunocytochemical strategies, and common diagnostic pitfalls encountered in the evaluation of non-small cell lung carcinoma, small cell lung carcinoma, neuroendocrine tumors, secondary pulmonary neoplasms, and uncommon thoracic entities in endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration and fine-needle aspiration samples. Particular emphasis is placed on the appropriate use of limited immunohistochemical panels to optimize tumor subtyping while preserving material for molecular testing. Diagnostic challenges such as crush artifact, necrosis, reactive mimics, overlapping morphologic patterns, and the risk of misclassification of rare tumors are addressed with practical guidance for differential diagnosis. By integrating morphologic assessment with ancillary testing, cytopathologists can achieve accurate tumor subtyping, distinguish mimics, and provide precise diagnoses that guide clinical management and selection of targeted therapies.

papers.title: The Diagnostic Value of EZH2 in Distinguishing NET G3 from NEC: An Immunohistochemical Study of 1618 Neuroendocrine Neoplasms of Various Origins and Grades
papers.abstract: The distinction between well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumours of grade 3 (NET G3) and poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NEC) guides treatment but remains challenging. We evaluated Enhancer of Zeste Homolog 2 (EZH2) immunohistochemistry as a supportive marker in 1618 neuroendocrine neoplasms (NEN) from ten centres, including 1083 NET G1/G2 and pulmonary carcinoids, 56 NET G3, 443 NEC and 36 medullary thyroid carcinomas and pheochromocytomas/paragangliomas, using the H-score with three expression groups (low < 100, intermediate 100–200, high > 200). EZH2 expression was low in 99.2% of NET G1/G2 and carcinoids and in all medullary thyroid carcinomas and pheochromocytomas/paragangliomas. NET G3 were EZH2-low in 67.9%, intermediate in 23.2% and high in 8.9% of cases, whereas large and small cell NEC were high in 52.2%, intermediate in 34.0% and low in 13.8% (p < 0.001). Low EZH2 expression supported NET G3 with a specificity of 86.2% (positive likelihood ratio 4.9), high expression supported NEC with a specificity of 91.1% (positive likelihood ratio 5.8), and intermediate expression was non-discriminatory. In an exploratory subset, EZH2 and p53/RB1 immunohistochemistry provided complementary information. EZH2 expression was associated with overall survival across the cohort but not within NET G3 or NEC. EZH2 is a simple supportive marker for the distinction of NET G3 and NEC: low expression supports NET G3, high expression supports NEC, and intermediate expression should be resolved by morphology and the established markers.

papers.title: Carotid body carcinoma in a French bulldog treated with toceranib phosphate.
papers.abstract: Carotid body tumors are rare neuroendocrine neoplasms in dogs, and evidence-based treatment options for malignant or unresectable cases remain poorly defined. An 8-year-old castrated male French bulldog was presented with a large cervical mass accompanied by progressive respiratory distress, neurologic abnormalities, and exophthalmos. Computed tomography revealed multiple, highly vascularized cervical masses with extensive local invasion, including nasopharyngeal obstruction and intracranial extension. Partial surgical excision was undertaken for diagnostic purposes, and histopathologic examination confirmed carotid body carcinoma with intravascular invasion. Because of incomplete surgical resection and malignant features, targeted therapy was initiated. Based on in vitro chemosensitivity testing, toceranib phosphate was selected. Following treatment, clinical signs related to mass effect improved, nasopharyngeal obstruction was alleviated, and increased intratumoral necrosis was suspected on follow-up imaging. Adverse effects were mild and manageable. The dog remained clinically stable for ~5 mo after targeted therapy but was subsequently lost to follow-up. On a later follow-up via telephone, the owner reported that the dog had died 6 mo after initiation of targeted therapy. Key clinical message: This case suggests that toceranib may represent a potential therapeutic option for dogs with unresectable or incompletely resected carotid body carcinoma.
papers.journal: The Canadian veterinary journal = La revue veterinaire canadienne

papers.title: SDHB deficiency silences ABCB1 expression and confers therapeutic vulnerability across multiple cancer types
papers.abstract: Succinate dehydrogenase B ( SDHB )-deficient cancers, including pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma (PPGL), renal cell carcinoma (RCC), and gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST), exhibit aggressive clinical behavior with limited treatment options. To identify novel therapeutic vulnerabilities, we performed high-throughput drug screening using co-cultured human SDHB -deficient and SDHB -reconstituted UOK269 human renal cell carcinoma cells with dual fluorescence labeling. Several compounds displaying preferential cytotoxicity toward SDHB -deficient cells were known substrates of the ATP-binding cassette B1 (ABCB1) transporter, also known as Multidrug Resistance Protein 1 (MDR1). Accordingly, SDHB -deficient cells demonstrated markedly reduced ABCB1 expression, a phenotype confirmed across human SDHB -deficient PPGL, RCC, and GIST samples, but absent in IDH - or FH -deficient tumors. Mechanistic investigation revealed that KDM4A histone demethylase is downregulated in SDHB -deficient tumors, and KDM4A loss (or inhibition) is sufficient to reduce ABCB1 expression, globally increase H3K9me3 levels, and sensitize cells to cytotoxic ABCB1 substrates. TCGA analysis confirmed correlated KDM4A-ABCB1 expression in SDHB -deficient cancers, with ABCB1 levels predicting drug sensitivity across cancer cell lines. Clinical analysis demonstrated that SDHB -mutant PPGL patients treated with vincristine-containing chemotherapy exhibited significantly longer progression-free survival compared to non- SDHB patients. These findings establish a novel metabolic-epigenetic pathway linking SDHB deficiency to ABCB1 silencing and provide rational basis for repurposing vincristine, and related ABCB1 substrate vinca alkaloids, across SDHB -deficient cancer types; offering an alternative precision treatment approach for these challenging malignancies.

papers.title: H3K9me3 Regulates IFNγlow Tex Cell Differentiation to Promote Colon Tumor Liver Metastasis.
papers.abstract: Despite the breakthrough in immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) immunotherapy in human cancer, colon cancer, except for the small subset of microsatellite instable human colon cancer, does not respond to ICI immunotherapy. As liver metastasis accounts for more than 90% of human colon cancer cases and mortality, ICI efficacy is primarily a measurement of liver metastasis suppression. Using a colon tumor liver metastasis syngeneic mouse model, we determined that mouse colon tumor liver metastases not only do not respond to anti-PD-1 immunotherapy but also exhibit no susceptibility to tumor-specific cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) adoptive transfer immunotherapy. Analysis of human colon cancer liver metastases single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets revealed that histone methyltransferases of histone 3 lysine 9 trimethylation (H3K9me3) are upregulated in colon tumors and expressed in subsets of T cells in liver metastases of patients with human colon cancer. Targeted therapy with the H3K9me3-specific histone methyltransferase inhibitor F5446 suppresses colon tumor liver metastasis. scRNA-seq analysis revealed the accumulation of PD-1+Tim3+ exhausted T (Tex) cells in mouse colon tumor liver metastases, and F5446 treatment increased the level of IFNγhighPD-1low Tex cells. Furthermore, F5446 therapy increased IFNγhigh intermediate Tex (Tex-int) cells in human colon cancer patient liver metastases-derived xenografts (PDX) and suppressed PDX growth in humanized mice. In patients with human colon cancer, response to pembrolizumab is associated with tumor-infiltrating IFNγhigh Tex cells. Our findings determine that H3K9me3 promotes differentiation of Tex cells and targeting H3K9me3 is an effective approach to increase IFNγhigh Tex-int cells to reinvigorate CTL functionality to suppress colon cancer liver metastasis.

papers.title: [PD-L1 expression in brain metastatic lung adenocarcinoma: correlation of clinicopathological features with prognosis].
papers.abstract: Objective: To assess programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression in brain metastatic lung adenocarcinoma, and its correlation with clinicopathological features and patient prognosis. Methods: A total of 94 patients with pathologically confirmed brain metastatic lung adenocarcinoma diagnosed at the First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University between January 2019 and December 2024 were retrospectively collected. PD-L1 expression in these brain metastases was detected using immunohistochemistry. Additional 14 primary tumors from the same patients were analyzed for expression consistency. All patients were followed up. Results: The cohort included 58 male and 36 female patients, with an age of 64 (57, 70) years. All tumors were grade 3 invasive non-mucinous adenocarcinomas based on the updated International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer grading system. The high-grade components were present in over 80% of tumor tissues, including micropapillary (17 cases), complex glandular (42 cases), and solid (35 cases) subtypes. PD-L1 was positive in 50 cases and negative in 44 cases. PD-L1 expression was correlated with the absence of driver gene alterations (P=0.022) and solid histological subtype (P<0.001), while PD-L1 absence was correlated with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations (P=0.016). Among the 14 paired samples, PD-L1 expression was concordant in 11 pairs, with a strong correlation in expression levels (rs=0.86, P<0.001). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis demonstrated that patients with PD-L1-positive brain metastases had significantly poorer survival (P=0.034). Conclusions: PD-L1 positive rate in brain metastases of EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma is lower than that in EGFR-wild-type cases. PD-L1 expression shows a certain correlation between primary lung adenocarcinoma and corresponding brain metastases, with tissue heterogeneity existing between the two. PD-L1-positive expression is associated with poorer prognosis in patients with brain metastases.
papers.journal: Zhonghua bing li xue za zhi = Chinese journal of pathology

papers.title: PET in Theranostics: Patient Selection, Treatment Planning, and Response Assessment.
papers.abstract: Theranostics pairs molecular imaging with a therapeutic radiopharmaceutical directed at the same target, with PET assessing target expression, disease extent, interlesional heterogeneity, and FDG discordance. Three established applications are reviewed: PSMA PET-guided selection for lutetium-177-PSMA-617 in metastatic androgen pathway modulation-resistant prostate cancer, somatostatin receptor PET-guided peptide receptor radionuclide therapy in neuroendocrine tumors, and iodine-124/FDG PET within radioiodine therapy for differentiated thyroid cancer. Practical guidance covers patient selection, image interpretation, treatment planning, response assessment, and reporting. A key paradigm: diagnostic uptake confirms target availability but neither measures delivered dose nor guarantees response; biomarkers, dosimetry, and response frameworks remain variably validated.

papers.title: Long-term Disease Control After Probable Endobronchial Small-cell Transformation During Osimertinib Therapy for <i>EGFR</i>-mutant Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract:
Background/aim

Osimertinib provides durable progression-free survival in EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but acquired resistance is inevitable. Histologic transformation to small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a recognized resistance mechanism, typically presenting with widespread metastatic disease and a poor prognosis. Optimal post-transformation treatment strategies have not been established.

Case report

We report a patient with EGFR exon 19 deletion-positive lung adenocarcinoma who achieved prolonged disease control on osimertinib for mediastinal lymph node recurrence before developing a new endobronchial lesion in the left main bronchus. Rigid bronchoscopic resection and temporary airway stenting relieved the critical obstruction. Pathologic examination confirmed SCLC, and immunohistochemistry of both the initial adenocarcinoma and the endobronchial lesion demonstrated concordant p53 over-expression and loss of Rb expression, supporting a clinical diagnosis of probable histologic transformation. The patient was bridged to sequential chemoradiotherapy, followed by successful stent removal and the resumption of osimertinib, resulting in long-term disease control exceeding four years.

Conclusion

An individualized, multidisciplinary approach comprising rigid bronchoscopic resection, temporary airway stenting, chemoradiotherapy, and osimertinib resumption may achieve prolonged disease control in locoregionally confined SCLC arising during osimertinib therapy. Further case accumulation is warranted to establish optimal treatment strategies.

papers.title: High Level of Component C1q Binding Protein (C1QBP) is Associated With Poor Prognosis and Dysfunction of Mast Cells in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract:
Background

Component C1q binding protein (C1QBP) is known as an important regulator of mitochondrial plasticity and is involved in antitumor immune response in cancers. Nevertheless, its role in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) still remains largely unknown.

Methods

C1QBP expression in LUAD and adjacent normal samples was compared by Wilcoxon test, and the corresponding receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was used to estimate its diagnostic value. Associations between C1QBP expression levels and different clinical traits were analyzed by chi-square test; K-M curves were applied for analyzing survival differences, and univariate and multivariate Cox analysis were employed to construct the C1QBP-related nomogram model. Furthermore, GSEA and immune analysis were performed to explore the mechanism. Finally, rhC1QBP was applied to cultured mast cells in vivo to investigate its regulatory effect on mast cell dysfunction, and sh-C1QBP was injected into LUAD xenograft mice to explore the effect of C1QBP knockdown on tumor growth in vivo.

Results

The C1QBP expression level, with a preferable diagnosis effect, was significantly different between LUAD and normal samples, and was notably interrelated with gender, TNM stage, and Fustat in LUAD patients. LUAD patients with high C1QBP levels displayed lower survival rates. Our nomogram based on C1QBP expression and T stage displayed decent prediction capability. There was a significant difference in C1QBP expression in plasma cells, regulatory T cells (Tregs), activated CD4 memory T cells, resting mast cells, and eosinophils between LUAD patients and the controls. Upregulation of C1QBP with rhC1QBP treatment promoted mast cell ferroptosis through interacting with the Cullin3 protein. While Fer-1, a ferroptosis inhibitor, counteracted rhC1QBP induced ferroptosis in mast cells. Knockdown of C1QBP inhibited tumor growth in xenograft mice.

Conclusion

C1QBP may be a promising potential prognostic biomarker in LUAD and a potential therapeutic target by affecting the immune microenvironment of LUAD patients.

papers.title: Intramuscular Myxoma of the Shoulder in Neurofibromatosis Type 1.
papers.abstract:
Background/aim

Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is an autosomal dominant tumor predisposition syndrome. Characteristic tumors associated with NF1 can be traced to derivatives of the neural crest. Tumors of the sheath cells of peripheral nerves (neurofibromas) are particularly common in NF1. NF1 patients have an increased risk of developing malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNSTs). These lesions primarily occur along the trunk and extremities. This report aims to expand the diagnostic spectrum of soft tissue tumors in NF1.

Case report

A male patient with NF1 diagnosed in early childhood and a history of repeated surgical treatment for a facial plexiform neurofibroma (PNF) developed a rapidly growing, firm, protruding mass near the right shoulder joint over several months. Clinical examination and magnetic resonance imaging suggested a PNF; however, the biological nature of the lesion could not be determined conclusively. The tumor was surgically excised, and the postoperative course was uneventful. Histopathological examination revealed an intramuscular myxoma of the periarticular shoulder region. No recurrence was observed during two years of follow-up.

Conclusion

Myxomas are not among the characteristic tumors of NF1. It appears that the development of a sporadic myxoma in NF1 is very rare. In this case, the findings and symptoms resembled those of a nodular PNF. Only surgical removal and histological examination could reveal the true biology of the lesion in this case.

papers.title: Uterine Carcinosarcoma With an Adenosquamous Carcinoma and Low-Grade Endometrial Stromal Sarcoma-like Component: A Case Report.
papers.abstract:
Background/aim

Uterine carcinosarcoma, also known as malignant mixed Müllerian tumor, is currently regarded as a metaplastic carcinoma. The sarcomatous component usually consists of homologous or heterologous high-grade mesenchymal elements, whereas low-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma (LG-ESS) has not been recognized as a conventional component of uterine carcinosarcoma. This is a case report of an exceptionally rare biphasic uterine malignancy composed of an adenosquamous carcinoma and an LG-ESS-like stromal component with an extensive morphological transition.

Case report

A 55-year-old nulliparous woman presented with an endometrial mass involving the myometrium and the endocervix. Endometrial biopsy revealed atypical hyperplasia, and cervical punch biopsy showed adenosquamous carcinoma. Subtotal hysterectomy revealed a high-grade endometrioid carcinoma with extensive malignant squamous differentiation (descriptively termed adenosquamous carcinoma in this report). The epithelial component gradually transitioned into diffuse stromal proliferation, which was morphologically consistent with LG-ESS. The stromal component exhibited infiltrative myometrial growth, extensive lymphovascular invasion, diffuse CD10 and vimentin expression, and loss of epithelial markers, whereas the epithelial component showed CK7, PAX8, CEA, and focal estrogen receptor expression. Squamous cell carcinoma, LG-ESS-like stromal component, and transitional area showed block-type p16 positivity and wild-type p53 staining pattern. Postoperatively, the patient received concurrent chemoradiotherapy but experienced rapid disease progression with pelvic recurrence and metastatic lymph node enlargement. Targeted next-generation sequencing revealed microsatellite stability and wild-type BRAF.

Conclusion

Unlike previously reported synchronous or collision tumors composed of endometrial carcinoma and LG-ESS, this tumor demonstrated a continuous morphological and immunophenotypic spectrum linking the epithelial and stromal components. Although molecular confirmation of clonality was unavailable, the findings favored a single biphasic neoplasm with divergent differentiation rather than two independent tumors. This case expands the currently recognized morphological spectrum of uterine carcinosarcoma and highlights the potential role of epithelial-mesenchymal transition in generating an LG-ESS-like stromal component.

papers.title: Quantifying Patient Setup Error in Total Body Irradiation With Megavoltage Computed Tomography-guided Helical Tomotherapy.
papers.abstract:
Background/aim

In helical tomotherapy (HT)-based total body irradiation (TBI), geometric accuracy is essential because intensity-modulated dose delivery relies on steep dose gradients. However, residual site-specific setup errors (SEs) after routine image guidance have not been fully characterized. This study quantified residual translational SEs after megavoltage computed tomography (MVCT)-guided global bony registration and derived landmark-specific planning target volume (PTV) and planning organ-at-risk volume (PRV) margins.

Patients and methods

Twenty consecutive patients who underwent HT-based TBI as conditioning for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation were retrospectively analyzed. A total dose of 12.0 Gy in four fractions was delivered using separate head-first and feet-first plans. After routine MVCT-guided registration, residual translational SEs were manually measured in the left-right, superior-inferior, and anterior-posterior directions at predefined anatomical landmarks: mandible, bilateral shoulders, pelvis, bilateral knees, bilateral heels, lung, liver, and bilateral kidneys. Systematic and random errors were calculated for each landmark, and PTV and PRV margins were estimated using modified margin recipes.

Results

Eighty fractions were analyzed. The mandible and lung showed high reproducibility, with residual SEs within 5.0 mm in all directions. In contrast, the shoulders showed the largest PTV-related uncertainty, with estimated PTV margins exceeding 10.0 mm in the superior-inferior and anterior-posterior directions. The liver and kidneys showed marked organ-related uncertainty, particularly in the superior-inferior direction; PRV margins reached 9.2 mm for the liver and up to 9.8 mm for the kidneys.

Conclusion

Residual SEs in MVCT-guided HT-based TBI were strongly site-dependent. Larger uncertainties in the shoulders, liver, and kidneys indicate that site-specific PTV and PRV margins should be considered rather than applying uniform margins across the whole body.

papers.title: [Reappraisal of the value of CD30 testing in the diagnosis and treatment of lymphoma].
papers.abstract: CD30 is a pivotal immunohistochemical marker for the diagnosis of selected lymphoid neoplasms and an important biomarker that informs clinical consideration of CD30-targeted therapy. With the expanding clinical application of brentuximab vedotin (BV) and BV-based regimens in classical Hodgkin lymphoma, peripheral T-cell lymphoma, primary cutaneous CD30-positive T-cell lymphoproliferative disorders, and relapsed/refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, the clinical role of CD30 testing has evolved beyond conventional diagnostic classification to encompass therapeutic decision-making and laboratory quality management. This review integrates the 5th edition of the WHO classification of haematolymphoid tumours (WHO-HAEM5), the International Consensus Classification (ICC, 2022), pivotal clinical trials, and recent international consensus recommendations to summarize the expression patterns of CD30 across different lymphoma subtypes, principles for immunohistochemical interpretation, standardized pathology reporting, evidence supporting CD30-targeted therapy, and key quality assurance requirements for laboratory practice. Particular emphasis is placed on the following concepts: immunohistochemistry remains the preferred method for CD30 assessment; pathology reports should adopt a descriptive approach that documents the localization, staining intensity, proportion, and distribution pattern of CD30-positive tumor cells; the clinical benefit of brentuximab vedotin is not simply correlated with the level of CD30 expression, as some patients with low-level expression or even no detectable CD30 expression by visual assessment of conventional immunohistochemistry may still derive therapeutic benefit; and standardized pre-analytical handling, quality control, interpretation criteria, review procedures, and recognition of intratumoral heterogeneity should be incorporated into routine laboratory practice. Practical recommendations regarding CD30 testing workflows, quality assurance, common diagnostic pitfalls, and pathology reporting are also provided to facilitate standardized pathology practice, laboratory quality management, and multidisciplinary clinical decision-making.
papers.journal: Zhonghua bing li xue za zhi = Chinese journal of pathology

papers.title: Comparison of 68Ga-FAPI PET/CT and 18F-FDG PET/CT in gastric cancer: impact on metastatic detection and stage migration.
papers.abstract:
Objectives

To compare the diagnostic performance of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) PET/CT and ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT in patients with gastric cancer, with particular emphasis on metastatic detection and stage migration.

Methods

Fifty-two patients with histopathologically confirmed gastric cancer who underwent both 18F-FDG PET/CT and ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT were retrospectively analyzed. Primary tumor uptake, metastatic involvement, and tumor staging were evaluated for each modality. Detection rates for lymph node, peritoneal, liver, and bone metastases were compared. Diagnostic performance and stage migration between modalities were assessed. Quantitative parameters including standardized uptake value and tumor-to-background ratio were analyzed.

Results

⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated significantly higher uptake in primary tumors compared with 18F-FDG PET/CT (P < .001). Peritoneal metastases were detected in 30.8% (16/52) of patients on ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT compared with 13.5% (7/52) on 18F-FDG PET/CT (P = .004). Nodal metastases were also identified more frequently with ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT. Both modalities showed high diagnostic performance for liver metastases, while ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated slightly higher sensitivity for bone lesions and 18F-FDG PET/CT showed slightly higher specificity. Overall stage migration between the 2 modalities occurred in 25.0% (13/52) of patients, predominantly due to upstaging associated with newly detected metastatic disease. In subgroup analysis, 18F-FDG uptake tended to be lower in signet-ring cell carcinoma, whereas FAPI uptake appeared less influenced by histological subtype.

Conclusion

: ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT improves detection of metastatic disease, particularly peritoneal involvement, compared with 18F-FDG PET/CT in patients with gastric cancer and may contribute to more accurate disease staging.

Advances in knowledge

This study highlights the added value of 68Ga-FAPI PET/CT in identifying metastatic disease and altering clinical staging, particularly through improved detection of peritoneal involvement, which may impact treatment decision-making.

papers.title: HPV-Associated Non-Salivary Adenocarcinoma of the Oropharynx: A Case Series.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated non-salivary adenocarcinoma of the oropharynx is exceptionally rare and poorly defined. We report a multi-institutional series of 12 cases from 6 tertiary centers. Histologic, immunohistochemical, HPV testing, molecular, and follow-up data were reviewed. Among 11 patients with available sex data, all were men; the median age was 62 years (range: 46 to 70 y). The cohort comprised 9 primary oropharyngeal adenocarcinomas and 3 metastatic adenocarcinomas, including a right neck metastasis of presumed oropharyngeal origin and 2 distant metastases in patients with previously documented HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. Primary sites included the palatine tonsil or tonsil-palate region (n=7), base of tongue (n=1), and oropharynx, not otherwise specified (n=1). Among cases with available T-category, 5 of 6 were T3/T4. All tumors showed high-grade adenocarcinoma morphology without a recognizable squamous component, with infiltrative glandular, ductal, or cribriform architecture. Diffuse p16 expression was present in all cases, and high-risk HPV was confirmed by polymerase chain reaction or in situ hybridization. p40 was negative in the tumor cell population in cases 1 to 6, 8, 9, 11, and 12, whereas case 7 showed p40 and CK5/6 expression confined to abluminal cells. Molecular profiling in 2 cases identified alterations or variants involving PIK3CA and PIK3R1. Follow-up in 6 patients with primary tumors showed distant metastases in 3 and disease-specific death in 1. HPV-associated nonsalivary adenocarcinoma of the oropharynx is a diagnostically challenging tumor that expands the morphologic spectrum of HPV-related oropharyngeal carcinoma. Recognition requires exclusion of salivary-type and metastatic adenocarcinoma and confirmation of HPV association.
papers.journal: The American journal of surgical pathology

papers.title: <sup>68</sup>Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT for Detection of Locoregional Lymph Node Metastases in Gynecologic Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract:
Background/aim

Detection of locoregional lymph node (LN) metastases is a critical prognostic factor in gynecologic squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) is limited by insufficient specificity, potentially leading to overtreatment. We evaluated gallium-68 fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (68Ga-FAPI-04) positron-emission tomography (PET)/CT for the detection of locoregional LN metastases in this setting, using CT as comparator.

Patients and methods

In this retrospective single-center study, 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT scans of 15 patients with gynecologic SCC (nine cervical, six vulvar carcinomas; mean age 56.3 years, range=38-86 years) were analyzed. PET/CT and CT were read independently by two blinded readers. Histopathology and/or clinical and radiological follow-up (12-18 months) served as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance was calculated on a patient-based level; maximum standardized uptake values (SUVmax) were compared using Welch's t-test and the Mann-Whitney U-test.

Results

Histopathological confirmation was available in 12 patients; three were classified by follow-up. LN metastases were confirmed in five patients. 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT achieved a sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV) and accuracy of 100%. CT achieved a sensitivity and NPV of 100% but produced false-positive findings in three patients (specificity=70%, PPV=62.5%, accuracy=80%), caused by tattoo-associated lymphadenopathy, sarcoidosis and reactive nodal enlargement, none of which showed pathological tracer uptake. Metastatic LNs exhibited higher SUVmax (mean 23.2±6.0) than nodes false-positive on CT (mean 4.5±4.6; p=0.004 and p=0.036). Primary tumors were visualized in all patients undergoing initial staging; peritoneal nodules down to 7 mm were detected.

Conclusion

In this small cohort, 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT showed a higher observed specificity than contrast-enhanced CT for the detection of locoregional LN metastases in gynecologic SCC, with no false-negative cases observed.

papers.title: Prognostic Value of Histology-specific Ki-67 Labeling Index Cutoffs in Stage I-III Non-small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.abstract:
Background/aim

Although the Ki-67 labeling index (LI) is widely used as a marker of tumor proliferative activity, its prognostic utility in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains uncertain because of heterogeneous study populations and the lack of standardized, histology-specific cutoff values.

Patients and methods

We retrospectively analyzed 1,245 patients with completely resected pathologic stage I-III NSCLC. Time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis for postoperative recurrence within 5 years was used to determine Ki-67 LI cutoff values. Associations between Ki-67 LI status and recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models.

Results

Ki-67 LI was significantly higher in squamous cell carcinoma than in adenocarcinoma (median, 40.0% vs. 15.0%; p<0.001). Time-dependent ROC analysis yielded a cutoff value of 21.0% for the overall NSCLC cohort and histology-specific cutoff values of 13.0% for adenocarcinoma and 40.5% for squamous cell carcinoma. The corresponding 5-year area under the curves (AUCs) were 0.656 for the overall NSCLC cohort, 0.691 for adenocarcinoma, and 0.607 for squamous cell carcinoma. After multivariable adjustment, high Ki-67 LI was independently associated with poorer RFS in the overall NSCLC cohort [hazard ratio (HR)=1.40; 95% confidence interval (CI)=1.11-1.77; p=0.005], adenocarcinoma cohort (HR=1.57; 95%CI=1.15-2.16; p=0.005), and squamous cell carcinoma cohort (HR=1.82; 95%CI=1.22-2.73; p=0.004). High Ki-67 LI was also independently associated with poorer OS in the overall NSCLC and adenocarcinoma cohorts, but not in the squamous cell carcinoma cohort.

Conclusion

High Ki-67 LI was independently associated with an increased risk of postoperative recurrence in both adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma. Histology-specific cutoffs derived by time-dependent ROC analysis may support Ki-67-based postoperative risk stratification in resected NSCLC.

papers.title: Beyond breathing: Lung as a sensory organ.
papers.abstract: The lung, one the largest branching organs in our body and vital for survival at first breath, is commonly known as the gas exchange organ. Recent novel findings on lung sensing cells, molecules, and lung-brain crosstalk in the emerging discipline of interoception have highlighted the consideration of the lung as a sensory organ. Acknowledging the central importance of lung sensing to human health and disease, the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute convened a workshop to synthesize the past, current, and future of lung sensing research, with in-person presentations by approximately 20 interdisciplinary experts and a large virtual audience. Here, we highlight the key topics discussed and summarize a blueprint for the future in this important field.
papers.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology

papers.title: An Immune-Metabolic Signature Reveals Prognostic Stratification and Tumor Microenvironment Features in Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer progression reflects coupled immune and metabolic reprogramming, but biomarkers that capture this interplay and provide additional prognostic information beyond routine clinicopathological assessment remain limited. We developed an 11-gene immune-metabolic risk Score in TCGA-BRCA (n = 1099) by integrating C7 immune signatures and KEGG metabolic pathways through Cox and LASSO-Cox modeling. The fixed model was applied without retraining to three public cohorts and an independent institutional cohort of 146 patients from Harbin Medical University Cancer Hospital. The score consistently stratified overall survival across independent cohorts and provided additional prognostic information beyond conventional clinicopathological variables. Integrative analyses showed that high-risk tumors were characterized by enhanced cell-cycle and metabolic activation, reduced lymphocyte-associated immune features, and monocytic-lineage enrichment. At single-cell resolution, high-score cancer-associated fibroblasts exhibited enhanced extracellular-matrix remodeling, inflammatory iCAF activity, and TGF-β-associated immunosuppressive programs. In an exploratory pembrolizumab-containing cohort, lower pretreatment scores were associated with pathological complete response and immune-active transcriptional programs; however, these findings do not establish the score as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy benefit. The 11-gene immune-metabolic risk Score provides complementary prognostic stratification beyond conventional clinical variables and characterizes a stromal-remodeled immune-metabolic state associated with adverse breast cancer outcomes.

papers.title: Fully Automated Segmentation of [<sup>18</sup>F]FDG and [<sup>68</sup>Ga]/[<sup>18</sup>F]PSMA PET/CT Images via Data-Centric Deep Learning.
papers.abstract: The purpose of this study was to develop and validate lesion identification in oncologic nuclear imaging (LION), an open-source PET-only tumor segmentation pipeline for [18F]FDG and prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted PET/CT, and to investigate how training data characteristics influence segmentation performance. Methods: In this retrospective multicenter study, 5209 [18F]FDG PET/CT scans spanning 19 disease types and 2046 PSMA-targeted PET/CT scans were used to train PET-only segmentation models. Tumor segmentation incorporated organs with physiologic uptake as auxiliary classes to enable PET-only inference. Tumor occurrence maps (TOMs) quantified tumor spatial diversity across the training data. For [18F]FDG, disease-specific and mixed-disease models trained on progressively larger subsets were compared to test whether increasing spatial diversity improves generalization. Scanner-related domain shift was analyzed using DINOv2 embeddings. Models were evaluated on multicenter holdout cohorts (616 [18F]FDG scans across 4 diseases; 443 PSMA-targeted prostate cancer scans) and compared with 3 open-source tools. Results: Organ context improved median Dice from 0.62 to 0.71 for [18F]FDG and from 0.75 to 0.83 for PSMA, on the complete holdout cohorts. Spatial diversity measured by TOMs was strongly associated with Dice (Spearman ρ = 0.80, P = 0.003). A mixed-disease model trained on 500 patients matched the performance of a lymphoma specialist model trained on 3031 cases. DINOv2 embeddings revealed scanner-induced domain shift between same-disease cohorts. LION achieved median Dice scores of 0.71 for [18F]FDG and 0.85 for PSMA and outperformed other open-source approaches on the model-comparison test set, which excluded the AutoPET test cases. Conclusion: LION enables PET-only automated segmentation for [18F]FDG and PSMA-targeted PET. Training data composition, particularly spatial diversity quantified by TOMs, was strongly associated with segmentation performance.

papers.title: Left Medial Liver Lobe Torsion Associated With Hepatocellular Carcinoma in a Pembroke Welsh Corgi: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Liver lobe torsion (LLT) is a rare, potentially life-threatening condition in dogs and is reported most often in medium- to large-breed dogs. Neoplasia-associated LLT is unusual, and detailed descriptions of LLT associated with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are scarce. A 12-year-old spayed female Pembroke Welsh Corgi (9.5 kg) presented with acute collapse after several months of progressive lethargy and inappetence. Laboratory abnormalities included increased alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase activities and C-reactive protein concentration. Computed tomography (CT) identified a 7.2 × 6.7 × 6.5 cm mass arising from the left medial liver lobe, a whirl sign at the base of the mass and a non-enhancing hypoattenuating region consistent with necrosis. Midline celiotomy and left medial liver lobectomy were performed without detorsion. Cytology of abdominal effusion was consistent with a culture-negative inflammatory exudate. Histopathology confirmed HCC with extensive necrosis, and the examined surgical margin was free of neoplastic cells. The dog recovered uneventfully, was discharged on postoperative Day 4 and had no recurrence of clinical abnormalities at 1-year follow-up. This case highlights the apparent association between HCC and LLT and the unusual location of the torsion axis at the base of the mass rather than at the hepatic hilus, although causality cannot be established from a single case. CT visualisation of the whirl sign at this atypical site was instrumental in establishing the preoperative diagnosis and guiding surgical planning.

papers.title: Surgical Management and Outcomes of Relapsed and Refractory Hepatoblastoma: An Institutional Case Series.
papers.abstract: Relapse occurs in 10%-20% of children with hepatoblastoma and is associated with inferior outcomes, yet standardized management remains limited. Defining risk factors and relapse patterns, as well as the role of surgery, particularly transplantation, is critical to optimizing survival. A retrospective review was performed of patients aged 0-18 years diagnosed with hepatoblastoma from 2007 to 2024. Demographics, tumor characteristics, treatment course, relapse patterns, and outcomes were collected. Analyses included univariable and multivariable logistic regression, Kaplan-Meier survival estimation, and log-rank testing. Among 135 patients, 98 (72.6%) achieved remission without relapse, 32 (23.7%) relapsed, and 5 (3.7%) experienced primary progression without remission. Older age, PRETEXT (pretreatment extent of disease) IV, metastatic disease at diagnosis, and macrovascular invasion were associated with relapse on univariable analysis, but only older age remained independently associated with relapse (adjusted odds ratio 1.27 per year, 95% confidence interval 1.05-1.53); PRETEXT IV and metastatic disease were not significantly associated with overall survival. Lung-only relapse demonstrated favorable survival (100% alive), whereas combined liver and lung or extrahepatic relapse had poorer outcomes (40%-44% alive), although survival did not differ significantly across relapse sites (p = 0.15). Of 54 liver transplant recipients, 44 underwent upfront transplantation, and 10 underwent salvage transplantation, with no significant difference in overall survival (p = 0.90), although the salvage group was small. Relapse or progression after upfront transplantation occurred in 27% of recipients; lung-only relapse again conferred favorable survival. Long-term survival is achievable in relapsed hepatoblastoma, particularly for isolated pulmonary relapse. Older age, likely a surrogate for adverse tumor biology, was associated with relapse but did not preclude survival when aggressive multimodal therapy was used. Salvage transplantation achieved durable survival in selected patients and should be considered for unresectable intrahepatic relapse when extrahepatic disease is absent or controlled.

papers.title: Dynamic control of carbon-ion radiation dose distribution amid respiratory motion challenges: A review of prediction research using geant4 and deep learning physics-constrained models.
papers.abstract:
Background

Carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) offers superior dose conformity and biological effectiveness; however, its precision is highly sensitive to respiratory motion, leading to dose uncertainty and interplay effects that compromise treatment accuracy.

Methods

A comprehensive literature synthesis was conducted on studies employing motion-resolved imaging techniques (e.g. SMEIR), dynamic dose prediction, 4D robust planning, and hybrid adaptive methods for CIRT. The study emphasised the use of Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations combined with deep learning models, including physics-informed neural networks, to simulate and predict dose perturbations caused by respiratory motion. This review also examined clinical treatment planning systems, radiobiological modelling, and adaptive strategies to mitigate the effects of motion.

Results

The integration of Geant4 with deep learning enabled high-fidelity, computationally efficient dose prediction under respiratory motion, improving accuracy in dose localization and adaptation. Motion management techniques such as respiratory gating, rescanning, and 4D robust optimization demonstrated enhanced tumor control and normal tissue sparing. Hybrid models combining Monte Carlo data and AI inference show promise for near-real-time adaptive therapy. Despite these advances, challenges remain, including limited motion-rich datasets, computational demands for real-time recalculations, and the complexity of incorporating variable relative biological effectiveness (RBE) into adaptive planning.

Conclusions

Combining Geant4-based Monte Carlo simulations with deep learning frameworks shows emerging promise for controlling carbon ion dose distributions amid respiratory motion, though direct clinical validation for this combination remains limited. These hybrid models may enhance the precision and adaptability of CIRT, offering improved outcomes. Future efforts should focus on clinical validation, standardization, and overcoming computational and data limitations to facilitate clinical translation of motion-adaptive CIRT. These approaches remain at Technology Readiness Levels (TRL 3-5) and require prospective clinical validation before routine implementation.

papers.title: Survival factors in lung cancer patients with mutations in the <i>PROS1</i>, <i>SERPINC1</i>, <i>F2</i>, and <i>F5</i> genes.
papers.abstract:

Purpose

Thrombophilia genes contribute to tumorigenesis and thrombotic events in lung cancer, yet current treatments do not incorporate gene-specific strategies for F2, F5, PROS1, and SERPINC1. We evaluated survival in lung cancer patients with thrombophilia mutations.

Materials and methods

We queried TCGA-LUAD and TCGA-LUSC for primary lung cancers with F2, F5, PROS1, or SERPINC1 mutations. STAR RNA-seq expression was included in univariate and multivariate Cox models comparing patients with versus without thrombophilia mutations, adjusting for age, race, AJCC stage, primary site, treatment type, laterality, and treatment modalities. Hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals were calculated.

Results

We identified 569 patients with thrombophilia mutations and 850 without. Across all mutations, higher pathologic stage and right-sided tumors were associated with worse survival. F5 mutations were significantly associated with survival in middle-lobe (HR 1.49, p = 0.028), pleural (HR 1.33, p = 0.006), and upper-lobe (HR 1.20, p = 0.025) cancers. SERPINC1 and PROS1 mutations were associated with improved survival in upper-lobe cancers. Among upper-lobe cancers, African American patients with F5 mutations had worse survival by age at diagnosis (HR 1.01, p = 0.015) and race (HR 1.33, p = 0.024).

Conclusions

Thrombophilia mutations influence lung cancer survival and may help refine gene-targeted therapies.

papers.title: Vulvar Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans in a Postmenopausal Woman: A Rare Case Report and Insights Into Treatment.
papers.abstract: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) is a rare cutaneous fibroblastic neoplasm characterized by locally infiltrative growth, a tendency for local recurrence, and low metastatic potential. Vulvar involvement is exceptionally uncommon and presents diagnostic and therapeutic challenges because of both its rarity and the anatomical importance of preserving vulvar function while obtaining adequate oncological clearance. We report the case of a 56-year-old postmenopausal woman, para 4, with a BMI of 32 kg/m², who presented with a 2 × 3 cm non-tender, freely mobile lesion of the left vulva. Excisional biopsy demonstrated a proliferation of spindle cells in a characteristic storiform pattern, with diffuse CD34 immunoreactivity, confirming DFSP. The closest histological margin following the initial excision was 0.3 cm. The patient was subsequently referred to a gynaecological oncologist, and following a multidisciplinary discussion, she underwent wide local re-excision with bilateral inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy. Histopathological examination demonstrated clear surgical margins, while all 13 lymph nodes showed reactive changes without evidence of tumour involvement. The case was discussed with a radiation oncologist, and adjuvant radiotherapy was not recommended after complete surgical excision and in the absence of residual or regional disease. No systemic therapy was administered. The patient remained free of documented recurrence for more than three years. This case highlights the importance of considering DFSP in the differential diagnosis of unusual vulvar masses, obtaining histopathological confirmation, and achieving complete excision with negative margins. It also illustrates the value of multidisciplinary management in rare vulvar soft-tissue tumours.

papers.title: Primary Male Appendiceal Choriocarcinoma With Background of Low-Grade Appendiceal Mucinous Neoplasm: Diagnostic Challenges and Poor Prognosis.
papers.abstract:
Background/aim

Choriocarcinoma is a highly aggressive trophoblastic malignancy that is most commonly gestational in origin. Non-gestational choriocarcinoma in the male gastrointestinal tract is extremely rare, and primary appendiceal involvement is exceptional.

Case report

We report such a case of a 75-year-old male who presented to the emergency room with severe abdominal pain. Physical examination indicated possible acute appendicitis suspicious for perforation, and computed tomography (CT) scans revealed a 7.5 cm mass in the lower right quadrant as well as numerous liver hypoechoic nodules. No lesions/nodules were identified in his testicles or mediastinum. Emergency surgery with right hemicolectomy and concurrent liver biopsy was performed. Pathology gross exam revealed a 7.5 cm appendiceal mass with associated appendiceal perforation. Histologically, the tumor showed a poorly differentiated carcinoma morphologically composed of syncytiotrophoblasts, cytotrophoblasts and intermediate trophoblasts with adjacent low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm (LAMN). The carcinoma cells were positive for cytokeratin 7 (CK7), beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG), GATA-binding protein 3 (GATA 3) and Sal-like protein 4 (SALL4). These features supported a primary appendiceal choriocarcinoma and the liver biopsy demonstrated metastasis of choriocarcinoma with extensive tumor necrosis. Post-surgery lab tests also revealed an exceptionally high serum β-hCG titer of 289,308 mIU/ml. The patient underwent hospice care after surgery and expired one month later.

Conclusion

This is the first documented case of male primary choriocarcinoma with background of LAMN and poor prognosis. Recognition of the three carcinoma components in combination with the corresponding tumor immunohistochemical markers is the key for the precise diagnosis.

papers.title: Hepatic Tumoral Calcinosis in a Patient With Obesity and Metabolic Syndrome: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Tumoral calcinosis is a kind of non-tumour calcium salt deposition, is an extremely rare disease, is also a soft tissue rare non-tumour lesion, belongs to the autosomal dominant genetic disease, mostly occurring in adolescents, seldom exceeding the age of 50 years, with a similar proportion of men and women, and its tumoral calcinosis occurs in the bone and joint parts, especially located in the femur rotator cuff, the elbow, the lateral part of the shoulder and the hip parts, which is manifested as it is characterised by painless subcutaneous calcified masses around the joints, which slowly increase in size, with a history of up to several years, and generally without obvious clinical symptoms. Therefore, this disease usually occurs in the bone and joints, and less frequently in the parenchymal organs. In this paper, we present a case of tumoral calcinosis in the liver, in which the patient was found to have a 24-year-old male presented with a 9-day history of a space-occupying lesion in the left lateral segment of the liver adjacent to the gastric curvature, accompanied by vague abdominal pain on satiety, without nausea, vomiting, chills, fever, or jaundice. Imaging features, laboratory tests and pathological findings confirmed our diagnosis, and a good outcome was achieved by surgical resection of tumoral calcinosis in the liver.

papers.title: The genomic afterlife of cancer therapy.
Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasonography of Orbital and Intraocular Pathologies in 24 Dogs and 6 Cats.
papers.abstract:
Objective

Contrast-enhanced ultrasonography (CEUS) is a noninvasive and relatively safe imaging technique to assess ocular perfusion, showing high sensitivity and specificity for tumor characterization in human oncology, while reports on its application in canine and feline diseased eyes are limited. This study aimed to describe the CEUS features of orbital and intraocular pathologies in dogs and cats in order to evaluate its diagnostic value in detecting and characterizing various lesions.

Animal studied

CEUS examinations of 30 animals (24 dogs, 6 cats) were evaluated retrospectively.

Procedures

Following B-mode ultrasonography, CEUS examinations utilizing sulfur hexafluoride were performed. Pathologies were categorized in one of the following groups: orbital neoplastic lesions, orbital inflammatory lesions, intraocular neoplastic lesions, intraocular inflammatory lesions and retinal detachment. Qualitative perfusion parameters, contrast intensity, enhancement pattern, perfusion type and time to wash-in and wash-out were evaluated.

Results

CEUS detected vascularization in orbital and intraocular pathologies, with variable enhancement characteristics. Persistent vascularization was observed in all cases of retinal detachment. In orbital and intraocular neoplastic lesions, CEUS improved lesion localization, assessment of interactions with surrounding tissues and tissue perfusion. For inflammatory pathologies such as abscesses, myositis, and steatitis, the additional diagnostic value of CEUS compared to B-mode ultrasonography was limited.

Conclusion

Findings indicated that CEUS could identify a variety of orbital and intraocular pathologies and provided additional diagnostic information to B-mode ultrasonography, particularly for assessing neoplastic lesions and retinal detachments. CEUS has the potential to enhance ophthalmic ultrasonography in differentiating specific pathologies. Prospective studies are warranted to further evaluate its clinical use.

papers.title: LncRNA A1BGAS1 Serves as a Tumor Suppressor in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer by Modulating the Expression of miR-3942-5P.
papers.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), the leading contributor to global cancer mortality, is associated with a notably unfavorable prognosis. This study aims to explore the regulatory interaction between A1BG-AS1 and miR-3942-5p and its molecular mechanisms. The level of A1BG-AS1 and miR-3942-5p in both tumor tissues and cell lines (BEAS-2B, A549, H226) were measured using qPCR. Functional effects of A1BG-AS1 overexpression in NSCLC cells were evaluated through CCK-8, flow cytometry, and Transwell assays. The interaction between A1BG-AS1 and miR-3942-5p was validated through dual-luciferase reporter assays and rescue studies. A1BG-AS1 expression was markedly reduced in both NSCLC tissues and cell lines. A1BG-AS1 expression was significantly associated with various clinical parameters. Overexpression of A1BG-AS1 suppressed NSCLC cell function. Mechanistically, A1BG-AS1 interacted with and negatively regulated miR-3942-5p, and the antitumor effects of A1BG-AS1 overexpression were reversed by miR-3942-5p mimics.A1BG-AS1 inhibits NSCLC tumor progression by targeting miR-3942-5p.

papers.title: Investigating Risk Factors for Delayed Melanoma Recurrence Beyond 5 Years Post-Primary Tumor Diagnosis.
papers.abstract:
Background

Patients undergoing treatment for cutaneous melanoma are generally considered cured after a period of 5 years, since most recurrences manifest within three to 5 years. However, some patients can present with a delayed recurrence of melanoma beyond a 10-year timeframe.

Objective

To identify clinicopathologic factors associated with survival in patients with cutaneous melanoma who developed metastatic recurrence at least 5 years after primary diagnosis.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study of 30 patients with cutaneous melanoma developing metastatic recurrence at least 5 years post-diagnosis. The cohort contained 18 women and 12 men (mean age 50.2; range 25-76). Variables included age, sex, BRAF status, site, melanoma subtype, Breslow thickness, ulceration, Clark level, regression, and recurrence localization. Overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and post-recurrence survival (PRS) were evaluated via Cox proportional hazards models.

Results

Mean OS, PFS, and PRS were 168.7, 130.4, and 43.7 months, respectively. Eight patients (27%) died. Tumors averaged 2.61 mm Breslow thickness; 50.0% were BRAF-mutant, 53.3% ulcerated, and 50.0% truncal. Recurrences were locoregional (cutaneous, subcutaneous, in-transit, nodal) in eight (26.7%) and distant in 21 (70.0%); one lacked data. Female sex predicted better univariate OS (HR 0.055, 95% CI 0.01-0.47; p = 0.008) and multivariate PFS (HR 0.364, 95% CI 0.14-0.93; p = 0.035). Increasing age predicted shorter multivariate PFS (HR 1.072, 95% CI 1.03-1.12; p = 0.001). Histologic regression (HR 3.557, 95% CI 1.04-12.17; p = 0.043) and BRAF status (HR 0.413, 95% CI 0.18-0.94; p = 0.034) independently impacted PFS. Kaplan-Meier showed longer OS and PFS in women, and longer PFS in patients younger than 50 years.

Conclusions

Delayed recurrence can manifest over a decade post-diagnosis. Female sex and younger age correlate with favorable survival. These findings underscore the necessity of continued clinical vigilance and patient counseling beyond 10 years, although larger cohorts are needed to validate late-recurrence risk stratification.

papers.title: Synthetic MRI from radiotherapy planning CT images for Head-and-Neck Cancer.
papers.abstract:
Background

Computed Tomography (CT) provides geometric accuracy and electron density information essential for radiotherapy planning; however, it offers limited soft-tissue contrast. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) improves tumor visualization but introduces registration uncertainties when acquired separately from the radiotherapy planning CT (pCT). Cross-modality image synthesis enables the generation of synthetic MRI (sMRI) directly from pCT and may combine the strengths of both modalities, reducing reliance on MRI access.

Purpose

We propose a two-stage deep-learning framework for generating sMRI from pCT image-sets specifically in head-and-neck (H&N) cancers, providing soft-tissue contrast comparable to ground-truth MR images (gtMRI).

Methods

This study included 60 patient cases with H&N cancer treated with radical radiotherapy between March 2022 and April 2024 for model development (50 for training, 10 for validation), plus 10 additional cases, independent of the development cohort for testing. All patients underwent a standard, non-contrast pCT scan followed by an MRI acquired on a 3T Siemens MR simulator. Images were deformably-registered, yielding 10,000 matched CT-MRI slice-pairs for model training. The proposed model utilizes a two-stage architecture, a Pix2Pix conditional generative adversarial network (GAN) for coarse sMRI synthesis, followed by a conditional diffusion model for refinement. To test the model's robustness, 10 patient cases with both pCT and contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) were used to generate sMRI. Model performance was assessed using structural similarity index (SSIM), multi-scale structural similarity index (MS-SSIM), mean absolute error (MAE), and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR). In addition, the geometric agreement of the primary (GTVp_70) and nodal (GTVn_70) gross tumor volumes delineated on sMRI vs. gtMRI was independently assessed by two radiation oncologists (ROs) using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), and average symmetric surface distance (ASSD).

Results

The average MS-SSIM, SSIM, MAE and PSNR for pCT-derived sMRI were 0.82 ± 0.02, 0.70 ± 0.03, 0.05 ± 0.01, and 20.42 ± 0.66 dB, respectively. The mean MS-SSIM and SSIM values for ceCT-derived sMRI were 0.02 lower than those for the corresponding pCT-to-sMRI metrics. For the contour-based evaluation, sMRI-derived GTV contours achieved a mean DSC of 0.56 and 0.60 for GTVp_70, and 0.72 and 0.74 for GTVn_70 across the two ROs, relative to gtMRI contours.

Conclusion

Our proof-of-concept study demonstrates the feasibility of pCT-derived sMRI for H&N cancers using a deep-learning framework. The model produces grayscale patterns and soft-tissue contrast that closely resemble the gtMRI.

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy of Intratumoral MEDI1191, an IL12 mRNA Lipid Nanoparticle, plus Intravenous Durvalumab in Patients with Advanced Solid Tumors: A First-in-Human Study.
papers.abstract:
Purpose

MEDI1191 is a lipid nanoparticle-formulated messenger RNA (mRNA) designed to induce local interleukin (IL) 12 production and intensify antitumor T-cell responses. We report dose-escalation results from a first-in-human, open-label, phase I study of intratumoral MEDI1191 plus intravenous durvalumab (NCT03946800).

Patients and methods

Patients were ≥18 years with advanced/metastatic solid tumors and had progressed on ≥1 line of prior therapy (immunotherapy permitted). Cutaneous/subcutaneous (parts 1A and 1B) or deep-seated lesions (part 1D) were injected; patients had ≥1 noninjected lesion measurable per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST v1.1). Target lesions were noninjected. MEDI1191 and durvalumab were given sequentially (part 1A) or concurrently (parts 1B and 1D). Primary objectives were safety and determination of maximum tolerated dose (MTD). Secondary objectives included efficacy.

Results

As of February 27, 2023, 61 patients were treated. Patients had a median of four prior regimens (range, 1-17); 39 (63.9%) received prior anti-programmed cell death protein 1/programmed cell death ligand 1 [PD-(L)1] immunotherapy. Treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAE) occurred in 96.7% of patients, and 41.0% experienced grade 3/4 TEAEs. There were no dose-limiting toxicities. The MTD was not reached. The objective response rate was 9.8%, including 1 confirmed complete response and 5 confirmed partial responses (PR). The duration of response was 2.7 to 22.3 months; the median was not reached. Responses occurred in injected lesions, local noninjected lesions, and distant lesions. Three of the 39 patients with prior anti-PD-(L)1 therapy had PRs.

Conclusions

MEDI1191 and durvalumab were tolerated. Preliminary antitumor activity was encouraging in these heavily pretreated patients, including patients previously treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors.

papers.title: Multiomics Dissection of Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer (EOCRC) Reveals an Immunosuppressive Microenvironment and Identifies FAT3 Mutation as a Biomarker of Hot-Like Immune Features.
papers.abstract: Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) exhibits distinct clinical and biological features compared with late-onset CRC (LOCRC), yet its genomic architecture and immune microenvironmental determinants remain incompletely characterized. Here, we integrated multiomics discovery analyses of 69 EOCRC and 461 LOCRC patients from the TCGA cohort, complemented by independent validation, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and systems-level network analysis. We identified 10 genes significantly enriched for mutations in EOCRC, including ANXA7, ZNF267, and POLQ, which displayed distinct domain-specific clustering and were validated in an external cohort. Mutational signature decomposition showed that EOCRC was associated with an SBS87-like signature, whereas LOCRC was dominated by SBS1; because TCGA lacks detailed treatment history, this SBS87-like inference should not be interpreted as direct evidence of prior thiopurine exposure. Immunologically, EOCRC displayed an immunosuppressive microenvironment characterized by elevated regulatory T cells, resting NK cells, and tighter immune-stromal coupling, as further supported by spatial transcriptomic analysis. Single-cell atlas analysis identified M2-polarized, SPP1-expressing macrophage subsets in EOCRC. Weighted gene coexpression network analysis identified a mitochondrial-ribosomal biogenesis module as the transcriptional hallmark of EOCRC. Finally, random forest analysis identified FAT3 mutations as a genomic correlate of a hot-like, immune-activated phenotype in EOCRC. Integrative single-cell analysis localized FAT3 predominantly to cancer-associated fibroblasts, especially myofibroblasts, and an in silico FAT3 perturbation analysis suggested potential downstream programs involving extracellular matrix remodeling, inflammatory signaling, chemokine response, and mitotic spindle regulation. These findings delineate age-stratified genomic and microenvironmental features of EOCRC and generate testable hypotheses for future functional and clinical validation.

papers.title: Further Insights Into the Mechanisms of Lymph Node Metastasis.
papers.abstract: Metastasis of malignant tumors arising from epithelial organs to sentinel lymph nodes has important implications for prognosis, staging, and therapeutic decision-making. Recent insights into anatomic pathways, pathogenesis, molecular interactions, and genetic factors have encouraged scientists and clinicians to develop drugs that target mechanisms of lymph node metastasis. We summarize important aspects of the vast literature that pertains to these mechanisms, focusing on five phases that implicate invasion through the epithelial basement membrane and tumor microenvironment, into initial lymphatics, and, after flow through lymphatic trunks, into the sentinel lymph node. Valuable information regarding tumor cell-directed motility, lymphangiogenesis, host cells that enhance metastasis, immune responses to tumor antigens, and tumor-induced changes in sentinel lymph node(s) provides a promising avenue for the continued development of new therapeutic approaches to prevent and treat metastasis. This article reviews these aspects by synthesizing current scientific and clinical advances and translating them for medical professionals.

papers.title: Integrative Transcriptional and Chromatin Analyses Reveal Enhancer-Mediated Regulatory Programs Driving Breast Cancer Metastasis.
papers.abstract:
Breast cancer metastasis remains the leading cause of disease-related mortality, yet the regulatory mechanisms enabling tumor cells to adapt to distant tissue environments remain poorly defined. In this study, we generated a multiomic resource integrating transcriptomic (RNA sequencing) and chromatin accessibility [Assay for Transposase-Accessible Chromatin using sequencing (ATAC-seq)] profiles from estrogen receptor-positive primary breast tumors and matched liver and lung metastases obtained from the same patients, including diagnostic and postmortem specimens. This design enabled direct intrapatient comparisons of primary and metastatic regulatory landscapes. We identified extensive reprogramming of chromatin accessibility and gene expression in metastatic lesions relative to primary tumors, indicating widespread regulatory remodeling. Peak-to-gene correlation analysis uncovered thousands of metastasis-associated enhancer-gene linkages, with metastatic samples exhibiting significantly increased enhancer connectivity. These rewired enhancer networks preferentially targeted clinically relevant genes, including receptor interacting serine/threonine kinase 4, inositol-3-phosphate synthase 1, and Ras-related protein Rab-3D, which were associated with three or more enhancers in metastases but not in primary tumors. Furthermore, ATAC-seq footprinting combined with gene expression analysis revealed distinct, tissue-specific transcription factor (TF) activity profiles in liver and lung metastases, including ESR1, that were not explained by TF expression levels alone. Together, these data provide a resource of metastasis-specific regulatory elements and their cognate TFs, revealing new regulatory vulnerabilities that may be therapeutically exploitable.

Implications

These findings support a model in which breast cancer metastasis is driven by enhancer regulatory reprogramming, allowing tumor cells to adapt to a variety of microenvironments.

papers.title: ERK1/2 Inhibitor Ulixertinib in Pancancer Patients with BRAF Fusions or Non-V600E/K Mutations: Results from the NCI-MATCH ECOG-ACRIN Trial (EAY131) Subprotocol Z1L.
papers.abstract:
Purpose

Mutations in BRAF at codons other than V600 (non-V600) and BRAF fusions confer dependence on the RAF-MEK-ERK pathway. Subprotocol Z1L (EAY131-Z1L) investigated the clinical activity of ulixertinib (ERK1/2 inhibitor) in patients with tumors harboring these alterations.

Patients and methods

In this single-arm study, patients with BRAF non-V600 mutations or BRAF fusions were given ulixertinib orally, at a dose of 600 mg twice daily, continuously for each 28-day cycle until progression or intolerability. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR). Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), 6-month PFS, and overall survival (OS).

Results

Of the 34 eligible patients, the median age was 66.5; 50% were women; and 88%, 9%, and 3% were White, Black, and Asian, respectively. Seventy-four percent of patients had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1. The median number of prior therapies was 4. Tumor types included multiple gastrointestinal malignancies (n = 16), lung cancer (n = 3), and melanoma (n = 3). No patients achieved complete response or partial response, resulting in an ORR of 0%. Stable disease was the best response in 7 of 26 centrally confirmed cases. The median PFS was 1.7 months [90% confidence interval (CI), 1.1-2.2]; the 6-month PFS rate was 5% (90% CI, 0.6%-17.7%); and the median OS was 3.5 months (90% CI, 1.9-5.4). Twenty (57%) patients had grade 3 toxicity, and 1 (3%) patient had grade 4 toxicity as their worst toxicity; there was no grade 5 toxicity.

Conclusions

Ulixertinib had no demonstrable evidence of clinical activity in this small, heavily pretreated population of patients with tumors harboring BRAF fusions or non-V600E/non-V600K BRAF mutations.

papers.title: Stromal CD163-positive Macrophage Enrichment Is Associated With a FOXP3-skewed Immune Profile and Poor Prognosis in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract:
Background/aim

The prognostic significance of macrophage-centered spatial immune architecture in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains incompletely understood. We investigated the spatial distribution and prognostic relevance of CD163-positive macrophages and their association with T-cell subsets in ESCC.

Materials and methods

A total of 139 patients with surgically resected ESCC, including a primary cohort (n=89) and an independent validation cohort (n=50), were analyzed. Double immunofluorescence staining was performed to evaluate CD163-positive macrophages, CD8-positive T cells, and FOXP3-positive T cells in intratumoral and stromal compartments. Associations with clinicopathological features and overall survival were assessed. Public transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets were analyzed for external biological validation.

Results

CD163-positive macrophages, CD8-positive T cells, and FOXP3-positive T cells were predominantly enriched in the stromal compartment. Stromal CD163-positive macrophage infiltration was positively associated with both CD8-positive and FOXP3-positive T-cell infiltration and with an increased stromal FOXP3/CD8 ratio, indicating an inflamed but FOXP3-skewed immune phenotype. Compared to conventional T-cell-based indicators, stromal CD163-related immune features showed stronger and more consistent associations with poor overall survival and remained significantly associated with overall survival after adjustment for age and pathological TNM stage in separate multivariable models. These findings were reproduced in the validation cohort and supported by transcriptomic and single-cell analyses.

Conclusion

Stromal CD163-positive macrophage enrichment is associated with a FOXP3-skewed immune architecture and unfavorable prognosis in ESCC. Macrophage-centered spatial immune features may provide complementary prognostic information beyond conventional T-cell-based indicators and warrant further investigation.

trials.title: A UGT1A1 Genotype-Directed Study of Belinostat Pharmacokinetics and Toxicity
trials.conds: Carcinoma, Neuroendocrine; Tumor, Neuroendocrine; Tumors, Neuroendocrine; Neuroendocrine; Carcinoma; Small Cell; Receptors
trials.brief:
Background:

High-grade neuroendocrine carcinomas (HGNEC) are cancers that develop in different parts of the body, including the digestive tract, genitals, neck, and head. One drug (belinostat), combined with 2 other drugs (etoposide and cisplatin), is approved to treat HGNEC. But some people may have a gene variant that affects how quickly their body gets rid of the drug; these people may do better with different dosages of belinostat.

Objective:

To test higher or lower doses of belinostat based on gene variants in people with HGNEC.

Eligibility:

trials.brief:
This study will evaluate members in families with a history of small bowel carcinoid cancer to study the natural history of those family members that have the disease, determine ways to improve early detection by performing surveillance on those at risk but without disease and to identify the gene(s) that may cause the tumors. Familial carcinoid tumors usually originate in hormone-producing cells that line the small intestine or other cells of the digestive tract. The tumors are slow-growing and usually take many years before they cause symptoms. It is known that these tumors occur more often in some families and are then passed from one generation to the next by inherited genes.

Members of families, including all siblings and offspring in which two or more immediate blood relatives have had small bowel carcinoid tumors are eligible for this study. In some cases unaffected spouses of family members diagnosed with carcinoid cancer are also requested to participate by donating a sample of blood only.

Participants undergo a medical evaluation every 3 years during a 3- to 5-day hospital stay at the NIH Clinical Center. All participants have a personal and family medical history obtained and undergo a physical examination, blood and urine tests.

People who already have a small bowel carcinoid tumor or are at risk of developing a carcinoid tumor have some or all of the following procedures to determine the presence of carcinoid tumor and its (omit next two words- location or) spread to other areas of the body:

* Video Capsule Endoscopy: Visualization of the gastrointestinal tract by ingesting a disposable, "vitamin-pill sized" video capsule that has its own camera and light source.
* CT of the chest abdomen and pelvis with oral and IV contrast : X-ray examination of the chest, abdominal and pelvis organs.
* 18 FDOPA Positron emission tomography (PET) with CT for localization: Nuclear imaging scan to look at tumor activity.
* MRI Liver with contrast - to determine if disease has spread to liver
* Gallium 68 PET/CT-limited to individuals that have residual tumor.
* Clinical and research blood work

Should mid gut carcinoid tumors be found every participant will be assisted in determine what the best course of treatment will be for them.
